Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky.
  • It has been revealed that putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine.
  • Recent findings suggest that in July, Russia confirmed that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky. According to Putin, Russia has control of the city in the Donbas; the remaining civilian population, he claims, could be evacuated. It would take five days to clear the access roads. The Russian leader has suggested that human rights organizations from Ukraine and Russia and delegates from the foreign press be incorporated into the mission.

It has been revealed that putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine. Experts say that while Russia is indicating a readiness to make agreements, at the same time it is propagating its own depiction of the situation on the front line.

Recent findings suggest that in July, Russia confirmed that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof. Ukraine states the fighting there is still ongoing. Experts from the Ukrainian open-source interactive map of military operations project DeepState say that the city is still controlled by the Ukrainian army, but that the situation there is "extremely difficult.".

Responding to the proposal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told journalists: "Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city." He emphasized that Ukraine had always given the civilian population in Kostiantynivka opportunities to leave, and stated that Russia had used the temporary ceasefire in Oleshky to bring military equipment and weapons into the city.

Sources indicate that kostiantynivka is the southernmost city in the so-called Donetsk "fortress belt," which also includes Druzhkivka, Kramatorsk and Sloviansk. Taking Kostiantynivka would open the way for Russian troops to advance to Druzhkivka, and on to the conurbation of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk.

Oleksandr Kovalenko, a military expert at the Dmytro Tymchuk Center for Security Studies, a Ukrainian think tank, remarked Kostiantynivka's role is similar to that of Bakhmut, Avdiivka or Chasiv Yar — towns whose defensive installations were able to hold back Russian enemy forces for years.

It has been revealed that local authorities say the humanitarian situation in the city, whose population before the start of Russia's full-scale invasion was around 70,000, is catastrophic and that some 340 civilians remain. They add thatKostiantynivkahas no central water, electricity or gas supplies, there is no public transport, and since the spring of 2026 people have only been able to evacuate on foot.

"Those who stayed in Kostiantynivka need to be evacuated, they need a chance of a better life," military analyst Denys Popovych told DW. However, he added that an evacuation was virtually impossible without a ceasefire, as Russian troops had occupied the road between the town and Druzhkivka and drones were being deployed throughout the region. Ukraine, therefore, could not carry out such an operation unilaterally. "It still takes two to tango — to evacuate the people, that is," he said.

Industry observers note that kovalenko believes that Moscow is simply using the humanitarian problem for purposes of manipulation and to strengthen its negotiating position. The Russian army, he remarked, wants to gain time in order to reinforce units fighting in the vicinity.

According to recent reports, yevhen Zakharov, the director of the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group, has similar concerns. "I'm afraid that this proposal by the Russians has very different objectives to those they claim to pursue," he told DW. He described Putin's initiative as suspect, and stated the Ukrainian side should treat it with the utmost caution.

Kyiv is in a difficult position, as the idea of a mission for Kostiantynivka is also being pushed by US intermediaries. "If we reject it, they'll say to us: 'You're rejecting peace proposals, you're not taking care of your own citizens, why should we keep talking to you, Zelenskyy wants to continue the war.' This is precisely the calculation behind it all," said Popovych.

After the end of the ceasefire in Oleshky, which was in place from October 27 to November 1, the Ukrainian General Staff announced that, in that time, the Russians had rotated their troops, entrenched their positions, reinforced measures to repel drones and brought in ammunition.

Kovalenko is convinced that the reason Russia is proposing a ceasefire is because its army is gradually losing ground in Kostiantynivka. From Moscow's perspective, the Russian troops that are meant to be storming the city are in urgent need of reinforcements, which they can't get because of the fighting on the ground.

"If a so-called humanitarian mission were to take place in Kostiantynivka, it would be a disaster for Kyiv, because Russia would use that time to consolidate forces that would enable it to take the city," he warned.

Sources indicate that popovych, however, does not think Ukraine should reject the Russian proposal. In his view, Kyiv should base its tactics on experiences with previous ceasefires and insist on very clear conditions in advance. "If there is a ceasefire, soldiers currently at their posts should stay there and not move," he suggested.

Oleksandr Pavlichenko from the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union believes Ukraine should submit a counter-proposal, which envisages the withdrawal of Russian troops from the Ukrainian city and the unimpeded departure of the civilian population.

According to recent reports, the human rights activist said that, for a genuine humanitarian mission to be put in place, a strong, neutral third party should be brought in to supervise and ensure safe passage. In his view, the only party with such a mandate is the International Committee of the Red Cross. "If a proposal comes from only one side, and from a side such as Russia, it doesn't inspire confidence," he said.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Between now and then, Arsenal’s longest away day takes them just 22 kilometres to Brentford - Google Maps claims the average person could walk from the Emirates to the Gtech in under four hours, never mind a professional footballer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Having made their longest Premier League away trip of the season to Newcastle last week, Arsenal can settle into familiar surroundings for the festive period: the Gunners don’t leave London again until mid-January when they travel to Hull.

Between now and then, Arsenal’s longest away day takes them just 22 kilometres to Brentford - Google Maps claims the average person could walk from the Emirates to the Gtech in under four hours, never mind a professional footballer.

According to recent reports, that’s the third of 11 straight games in the capital for the Gunners, which will become 12 if they’re drawn at home in the third round of the FA Cup, beginning with Tuesday’s Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund. Recent history suggests an interesting theory about such home comforts.

It has been revealed that eleven games into their title defence, Arsenal sit second in the Premier League away table with four wins, one draw and one defeat from six games on the road. Not that it’s anything new for the Gunners to occupy such heights: they’ve boasted the top flight’s best away record in each of the last four seasons.

And that comes with the territory of being a London club. Across the last 10 Premier League campaigns not impacted by pandemic crowd restrictions (so excluding 2019/20 and 2020/21), only once have more clubs from London had a bottom-half away record than a top-half away record. That was last term, when four of the seven London clubs finished in the bottom 10 of the away table (Crystal Palace, Brentford, Fulham and West Ham).

In each of the other nine seasons in question, at least 57 per cent of the Premier League’s London clubs have finished with one of the best 10 away records in the division; in 2016/17, all five of them did (Chelsea, Tottenham, Arsenal, Palace and West Ham).

So, is it an advantage to be a London club?

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

There’s not really a simple answer to that question (sorry), but we can still pull together some interesting takeaways.

Sources indicate that this season, the average Premier League club will travel 153 kilometres for an away fixture. For two clubs, that average climbs to over 300km: the league’s two most north-easterly sides, Sunderland (350km) and Newcastle (347km), and the most south-westerly, Bournemouth (317km). Conversely, one side will travel a touch under 200km on average: Coventry (198km) – in that sense, you might consider the Sky Blues the ultimate Midlands club.

It has been revealed that but the top-flight’s six London clubs all sit in the bottom eight of the league in terms of average away travel distance, with Palace travelling the furthest (227km) and Spurs the least far (202km). And the very fact that those sides account for just over a quarter of the division means short trips are a regular occurrence.

And for Arsenal, this 11-match stretch that sees them go no further than Brentford could not fall at a better time than the notoriously hectic festive period – certainly when it comes to maximising recovery time between fixtures, which come thick and fast an average of one game every 4.2 days between now and January 5 (though it’s worth noting that turnaround is still below the UEFA-recommended minimum window of five days between matches).

Could the timing of Arsenal’s London residency, so to speak, prove crucial to another successful Premier League title push? Well, they’re already six points clear at the top and look like they could walk it, given Manchester City’s dramatic recent drop-off, but minimising time spent on the road during one of the busiest stages of the campaign seems unlikely to work to their detriment.

That being remarked, a quick word on Chelsea: the Blues have left London three times all season but are languishing in mid-table in the Premier League and are out of the Carabao Cup. So, maybe there’s something to be said for getting out of town on a more regular basis. Besides, it’s not like elite-level players these days are travelling in anything less than luxury, is it?

Haaland did raise a smile about the prospect of his impending battle with Arsenal defender Gabriel this weekend.

The Man City star has shown increasing dejected body language during games and has spent too much time recently with his head bowed and hand waving at team-mates.

Haaland talked about City needing to be at their maximum to take anything from the Emirates this weekend. Whether that is ‘fun’ or not is a different matter entirely, but what Enzo Maresca must demand more from all of his players. Even with 14 goals already this term, that includes Haaland.

He is leading from the front off the pitch. Standing in front of the cameras more than anyone else, facing up to the dipping form and taking on those responsibilities without complaining. Yet City need more of that leadership between the white lines from somebody who has drawn a blank in four of his last five club matches, despite scoring three times over the international break.

There is too much head bowing and hand waving at the moment.

The 26-year-old admits he has to give extra. And believes that the team are generally creating enough chances for him, even if the freewheeling attacking abandon of early season has vanished.

In a recent development, city's results are clearly affecting Haaland’s mood and that can be self-perpetuating. He admits that failing to reverse this run is hurting him. That is evident by watching his increasingly dejected body language during games and the frustration seen when he gestured at Abdukodir Khusanov as the defender dithered with a routine throw-in during Saturday’s draw against Fulham. It wasn’t the picture of a man happy with his lot.

Recent findings suggest that only Haaland will know whether that general angst is contributing to a lack of intensity in his own performances. Nobody has mentioned the striker carrying a knock, although Maresca has appeared focused on offering him rest whenever possible over the past three months.

According to recent reports, something is undoubtedly proving an obstacle for him. He’s insisted that it isn’t the guilty verdicts hanging over City and, listening to him, the gripes and disappointment look focused on City’s lack of control in games. It also cannot help that Haaland will feel aggrieved to have seen a goal on Saturday chalked off for a foul on Bernd Leno and then to have not been awarded a penalty for grappling on Tuesday night.

If both or even one of those decisions go his way, the interview that sparked concern with fans – one conducted almost immediately after full time when emotions are at their highest – would likely have been very different.

It has been revealed that city will have to cling on to the idea that a sullen Haaland is at least a Haaland who cares. And a Haaland who cares must surely dig them out of this hole, even if he cannot do that alone.

It has been revealed that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Tottenham teenager Luca Williams-Barnett has committed his future to his boyhood club by signing a new contract.

The 18-year-old caught the eye during his full Spurs debut in Saturday's 2-0 Premier League victory over Ipswich, striking after 15 minutes before driving forward from deep inside his own half to assist Dominic Solanke six minutes after the second-half restart.

With his previous agreement entering its final 24 months, Spurs have now moved to extend the youngster's contract.

"This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach, but this is only the start," the Academy graduate told the official club website.

"Spurs is a family to me. I have been here for so long – it’s a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

"The club has trusted and believed in me, now I’m ready to repay that.".

Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi believes far more is to come from the England Under-19 international.

"Luca is a player I think the world of, and I’m so happy that he has signed a latest contract," De Zerbi said.

"He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

"Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch, but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

"The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.".

Spurs sporting director Johan Lange feels "special talent" Williams-Barnett fully merits his fresh contract.

"Luca’s progression through the Academy to this point is a great example of what our pathway is designed to achieve and what is possible for young players here," Lange remarked.

"We are excited to watch Luca continue to develop and be an important player for the club, both in the present and the future.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Six months after the glory of that Europa League final, Aston Villa’s return to Istanbul proved a chastening night of disappointment.

Unai Emery’s team have undergone a significant rebuild since that stirring night in May and this was another occasion where Villa 2.0 were exposed as a work in progress.

Emery’s run without a win has extended to six matches in all competitions and Villa’s Champions League campaign does not promise to get any easier, with Paris St-Germain up next.

There was always likely to be a period of transition this season, as six of the heroes from the Europa League final’s starting XI were sold over the summer.

Despite some encouraging signs before the last international break, and three successive Champions League wins, Villa are now enduring a difficult run.

Their second-half performance in particular was poor, and Galatasaray secured victory with the evening’s first shot on target.

The deadlock is FINALLY broken 🙌 Deniz Gül gives Galatasaray the lead after a scramble in front of the net. 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/SplkgZC63p.

Sources indicate that emery was booked late on as his frustrations got the better of him. His team appear short of creativity and, when Nicolas Jackson struggles, are toothless in the final third.

Industry observers note that though Villa did frustrate the Turkish champions for long periods on a slow, substandard pitch, this was a second successive defeat in the Champions League. Emery now faces a daunting double-header against PSG and Borussia Dortmund. They may still have enough to qualify for the knockout stages, but Villa fans of a certain vintage will insist their team never do it the easy way.

Industry observers note that emery was unhappy with the performance of German referee Daniel Siebert and mentioned: “I am disappointed a little bit. After their goal, it was impossible to play. They wasted time. They added only five minutes. OK, finish the match. We don’t want to play more, I don’t think the referee was fair there. Two years ago we lost to Brugge and Monaco away [in the Champions League]. Today I can compare this match to those matches.”.

Sources indicate that alejandro Garnacho, the Chelsea loanee, did not travel and was absent from the match-day squad for the fourth game in a row. Emery said: “Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us.” It was far removed from the magical scenes of the Europa League showpiece across the city.

Villa’s fears before kick-off centred on the playing surface, with the pitch recently relaid after extensive maintenance, but it had no real impact on the result. Galatasaray defeated Liverpool twice in the Champions League at Rams Park last season and can be awkward opponents.

In a game of few chances, Villa were intent on frustrating both Galatasaray’s players and supporters by slowing the game down, restricting the home team’s threat by playing five in defence.

It has been revealed that galatasaray were lacking inspiration but were given an injection eight minutes into the second half. The flashpoint came after a crude challenge from Davinson Sánchez on Villa’s Brazilian winger Alysson.

It has been revealed that sánchez, the former Tottenham defender, escaped a booking but an angry John McGinn responded by colliding with Aleksey Batrakov near the touchline. Both players were given yellow cards by Siebert, and McGinn was infuriated that Batrakov avoided more extreme punishment for kicking out at him.

Recent findings suggest that that aggravation only served to fire up Galatasaray and there was a sense of inevitability to their goal 13 minutes from the end. Villa were under pressure and failed to clear a corner, with Deniz Gul punishing Jackson’s error to head the ball over the line after a deflection off Tyrone Mings.

Seven minutes of added time failed to spark Villa into life by creating a late chance and they returned home without registering a shot on Ugurcan Cakir’s goal.

According to recent reports, villa’s downturn in form continues with a Champions League defeat which owed everything to their shortcomings going forward. They settled well in a hostile atmosphere, but allowed all their possession to drift into sterility, and the second half was just plain poor. A low-quality game settled by a messy goal, but credit to Gul for putting his head where it hurts.

Villa will surely finish the week outside the top eight, with home games against PSG and Borussia Dortmund to follow.

The referee has allowed the game on beyond the five additional minutes, but a Harwood-Bellis loose pass stalls Villa in their own half.

They soon break out into midfield space though, but with all the time in the world Barkley’s pass was a touch behind Hemmings and Sanchez was able to get a toe to it.

Of all the venues in the Champions League where a referee might be inclined to blow his whistle as soon as possible, this might be the one so time is running out for Villa.

Lucas Torreira has taken a kick on the ankle, and he limps off to be replaced by Ilkay Gundogan, who has played just 75 minutes this season.

Villa then find some space down the left but Singo blocks Maatsen’s cross which was aimed towards Jackson.

Industry observers note that ross Barkley the fourth Villa player booked on the night. There will be five minutes added on, which surely does not represent all of the stoppages, but Uefa’s approach to timekeeping resembles freestyle jazz.

Industry observers note that villa eventually worked a position to cross the ball from that free-kick, but Lindelof’s header back into the six-yard box was too close to Cakir and the goalkeeper pounced on the ball. Time running out for Villa.

Villa have been sleepwalking to defeat throughout the second half, they have completely lost any assurance in their passing game. That was better, and Goretzka wins a free-kick in midfield which they are going to clip forward.

Buendia has been brought on for Kamara, but Hemmings shoots over when Singo was on the turf appealing for a foul not given. Villa have shown more intent in the last three minutes than the previous 30.

The goalscorer Gul is back on with a bandage around part of his face.

Things could have gone from bad to worse for Aston Villa because VAR checked for a Jackson red card for a high boot on Gul, but eventually the incident is cleared. Villa have 10 minutes plus stoppage time to salvage a result.

Mbaye with a dangerous ball into the box but he was offside in any case.

Industry observers note that villa undone from a corner, and the striker thrown on as a substitute has scored the game’s opening goal. Gul appears to have hurt himself in the process, he took a kick in the face from Jackson when planting his head on the ball. Villa lost the first contact at the near-post and from there it was a mess. Gul receiving treatment with blood streaming down his face.

Industry observers note that the deadlock is FINALLY broken 🙌 Deniz Gül gives Galatasaray the lead after a scramble in front of the net. 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/SplkgZC63p.

Tyrone Mings defends well but he cannot prevent Galatasaray winning another second-half corner.

Galatasaray with a double change: Sara and Ugochukwu on for Batrakov and Lemina.

Emery responds in kind: Hemmings and Barkley on for Manzambi and McGinn.

It has been revealed that aston Villa struggling to find any rhythm after another stoppage in the game, but Galatasaray are enjoying more of the territory. Nicolas Jackson has been a revelation this season but has been underwhelming in the second half.

Now Gortetzka is waved on by the referee, who made Villa wait because Gomes took too long to walk off the pitch. Suzuki commands his box in the air once again to climb a high ball launched into the mixer.

Alysson and Gomes are the players coming off for Mbaye and Goretzka, but the German midfielder has been to wait on the touchline by the referee much to Emery’s Fury. Gomes has already gone off, so Villa are down to 10. Bizarre officiating, not sure I can recall seeing that.

Now Galatasaray have a corner! But Villa clear at the near post.

Villa floundering and under pressure for the first time in the game, Mbaye and Goretzka are about to be introduced by Emery.

Galatasaray have a free-kick in a crossing position left of centre, but Akgun’s delivery floated over everyone in the box and Torreira is then penalised for a foul on Manzambi.

Galatasaray have made a change in their attack, with a more orthodox striker in Gul replaces Elmali, so Yilmaz moves out to the left. Torreira wins a foul in midfield, but Gomes and Kamara were convinced they had won the ball cleanly.

That aggro has given Galatasaray a lift and the noise is now increasing.

Villa need to keep their nerve here.

Recent findings suggest that villa have slightly lost their way in the last 10 minutes, they are not passing the ball with their early fluency and appear caught between holding what they have or pushing on for a goal. Maatsen the latest player guilty of a cheap giveaway.

Akgun reacts with fury after he is tripped on the sly by Alysson to stop a break away, and they square up to each other. Both players have been booked, so there have been five yellow cards so far.

Recent findings suggest that suzuki does well to claim a cross but he caught Elmali who stays down in the penalty area to receive some treatment. A little bit of needle in the game is welcome because neither team is creating much.

Galatasaray waste a corner, and then Villa spring a counter-attack despite Maatsen’s initial poor pass. Sanchez crashed into a challenge on Alysson, before McGinn returns the favour with interest on Batrakov. McGinn is booked for the tackle, Batrakov for his reaction. The Galatasaray player kicked out slightly after he was bodied by the Villa man. Both benches were up, but no further punishement for either player.

Jackson nods the ball down into a dangerous area but Bardakci clears for Galatasaray. Villa continue to dominate possession, Galatasaray keep going long towards Yilmaz to no avail. They are feeling the absence of Osimhen.

Industry observers note that very messy defending from Galatasaray and there are vociferous appeals for a Villa penalty after a lunging challenge in the box, but the referee and VAR decide there is nothing in it. The layer of sand under the top surface of the pitch is becoming increasingly visible as the game goes on.

No changes from either manager at half-time.

Unai Emery will be fairly satisfied with that first-half performance.

In a match of few chances, Villa have frustrated the home team and defended resolutely in the rare occasions Galatasaray have applied pressure.

The pitch is slowing the game down which is helping Villa. There was a weird booking for Nicolas Jackson late in the half so it would be no surprise to see him taken off by Emery either at half-time or very early in the second.

In a recent development, A controlled and composed 45 minutes from Villa, but in truth Galatasaray have put them under very little pressure. McGinn, Manzambi and Jackson have produced some smooth flicks and touches, but there has been a lack of devastation in the final third. That has been the missing element for Villa so far. For all the talk of the atmosphere, they should be beating this team.

Sources indicate that nicolas Jackson has been booked, and Alysson loses the ball cheaply to put Galatasaray away on the counter-attack. Mings is up early to head the corner away. The home team continue to look pretty toothless.

Industry observers note that elmali’s cross from the Galatasaray left is woefully overhit and Suzuki claims, but it was a poor pass from Harwood-Bellis that instigated the attack. Villa soon restore order with a spell of possession.

Unsurprisingly, the best pass of the match so far has come from Zion Suzuki.

The Villa goalkeeper has just pinged a pearler over 40 odd yards to Alysson on the right wing.

Galatasaray find some joy with quick switches of play with Villa’s defensive shape quite narrow, but Akgun’s chipped cross was overhit.

Joao Gomes then takes an extra touch inside his own box, but moves the ball on before he is caught in possession.

Torreira than clatters Gomes, not his first foul on the night, but somehow he escapes a booking.

McGinn is picking up some midfield positions that are hard for Galatasaray to pick up, but a couple of Hollywood passes from there have not come off.

Better attacking play from the home team, but Mings was well positioned to head clear a deflected cross.

Villa with another slick move, and this one had more attacking punch at the end of it. Maatsen delivered a wicked low cross and Manzambi was waiting for a tap-in but Sanchez made a last-ditch challenge. No doubt that Villa are the better team.

For a moment it looks as if Manzambi had missed a glorious chance but the flag belatedly went up for offside against Jackson who collected the ball wide right when well ahead of the play.

Villa are doing a very good job of frustrating both the Galatasaray players and their supporters so far.

They are slowing the game down and producing some neat interplay in advanced positions.

Johan Manzambi, in particular, is covering a lot of ground.

According to recent reports, suzuku rushes off his line to sweep up a through ball, but Alysson had also tracked a run all the way. Singo passes forward swiftly but Galatasaray’s playmaker Batrakov cannot put the ball under his spell.

John McGinn with a chance to deliver a free-kick from a crossing position, but Galatasaray win the header at the back post. Villa continue to be comfortable in the game, without really working the goalkeeper Cakir. The home crowd are restless, Galatasaray have yet to muster a menacing attacking.

Villa moving the ball well inside Galatasaray’s half with some neat interplay between Manzambi and Jackson when they are in close proximity, but there is no telling pass or shot at the end of the move.

Lovely turn from John McGinn between the lines but Galatasaray’s defender Bardakci intercepted his through ball. Manzambi started wide left on the team sheet, but Maatsen’s runs forward are allowing the Swiss to play in a narrower position.

Industry observers note that akgun wins a free-kick for Galatasaray, who have grown into the contest in the last few minutes. Torreira and Batrakov swapping positions in midfield, and Singo is an impressive player at right-back. The delivery from the free-kick is poor though.

Galatasaray did beat Liverpool twice in this competition last season so cannot be taken lightly tonight.

The pitch does appear to be cutting up a bit in some areas already.

Jackson perhaps unfortunate not be awarded a foul in the left corner, but this has been a bright start by Villa.

Their front players Manazmbi, Alysson and Jackson all combined in a one-touch move after Suzuki played long before the Villa striker was flagged offside.

According to recent reports, lovely pass from Zion Suzuki inside the opening minute, picking out Harwood-Bellis who was free down the right. He found Manzambi unmarked in the middle before Maatsen’s progress down the left was halted. Villa enjoy drawing a press, so it could suit them if the home team are aggressive.

Villa get the game under way, and from the aerial view you can see the seams between patches of the pitch.

A cacophony of hoots, howls and whistles will greet the Villa players, and the same will be true of their every touch of the ball. Aleksey Batrakov, likely to play in behind Yilmaz for the home team, has been identified as Galatasaray’s potential danger man.

Alejandro Garnacho has now been left out of the Villa squad for four games in a row.

He trained at Bodymoor Heath on Monday so does not appear to be injured.

It is looking pretty bleak for the Chelsea loanee, and the comparisons with Liverpool’s Harvey Elliott last season are impossible to escape.

Villa have made a solid start on their return to the Champions League, winning three and losing one.

Aston Villa supporters have happy memories of Istanbul after May’s Europa League final, and they return to face Galatasaray this evening in a fixture which could forecast their Champions League prospects.

It has been par for the course for Unai Emery’s team in Europe so far, with victories over Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking and a defeat at Barcelona aligning with the form book.

Nine points from 12 leaves them inside the top eight at the halfway stage of the league phase, but tougher challenges are ahead with PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come after tonight’s game.

Since a statement victory over Manchester City, it has been a frustrating time for Villa either side of the international break. They were dumped out of the League Cup by Bournemouth, were second-best in a home draw with Fulham, threw away a pair of two-goal leads at Old Trafford, and were held by Sunderland at the weekend.

Though Villa put six past Galatasaray’s city rivals Fenerbahce at Villa Park, away games against Turkish opposition can be different beasts, as Liverpool discovered in the last round of Champions League matches.

Galatasaray’s two major attacking threats, Victor Osimhen and Rafael Leão, are both absent with injuries. Davinson Sanchez and Lucas Torreira are former Premier League players in their squad. Galatasaray have won two of four Champions League games, losing to Barcelona and Sporting Lisbon, but they are top of the Turkish Super Lig.

Villa will be without right-back Matty Cash owing to a concussion sustained during the international break with Poland, but will hope to have Victor Lindelof available again after he missed the Sunderland draw with illness.

Emery’s team were unable to train at Rams Park yesterday in order to give a troublesome pitch maximum recovery time after emergency renovation work.

“If we could have trained in the stadium of Galatasaray, maybe we would have decided for the same situation, but it’s not changing our routine,” Emery noted. “How the pitch is going to be tomorrow is important, but it’s not an excuse because it’s [the same] for both teams. Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Discussions between Bayern Munich officials and Jamal Musiala’s representatives on Tuesday focused on the star player's health rather than his salary, according to the club's board member for sport Max Eberl.

The talks took place shortly before Bayern flew out for Wednesday's Champions League fixture against Lille in France. They follow recent criticism from global players' union Fifpro, which accused Bayern of "a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala" after he suffered seizures.

Characterising the meeting as "very, very constructive”, Eberl said the focus was entirely on Musiala’s recovery from a recent injury, in comments reported by the dpa news agency.

"Today it was about just how we want to get Jamal back on the field, just like before his muscle injury in the international break," Eberl stated. "That's the only task FC Bayern has currently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something.".

Prominent figures at Bayern had previously questioned whether Musiala could return to his previous form, suggesting the contract extension he signed last year might no longer reflect the player he has become.

The idea that terms could be renegotiated due to poor health drew rare, sharp criticism from Fifpro.

"Contracts are there to be respected," the players' union stated on Saturday. "An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.".

Musiala has featured rarely since collapsing during pre-season games in August and has also dealt with a muscle problem. He was nevertheless included in Bayern's 20-player squad travelling to Lille on Tuesday.

Social media posts previously published by Musiala stated he had been diagnosed with "absence seizures caused by a neurological dysfunction”, noting the condition was not a threat to his health and confirming his intention to continue playing.

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany, who has experienced his own health concerns this season before returning to the touchline last week, publicly backed Musiala in September, stating it would not be "a significant deal" if the seizures were to return.

What has happened to Senne Lammens this season?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that there were other factors that led to Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool besides Senne Lammens’ performance, like Leny Yoro’s red card after only eight minutes.
  • And yet in the post-match analysis, Manchester United’s first-choice goalkeeper still found himself scrutinised.
  • In a recent development, it wasn’t the first time a Lammens mistake has been highlighted this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there were other factors that led to Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool besides Senne Lammens’ performance, like Leny Yoro’s red card after only eight minutes. Down to 10 men for the majority of the match, Mauricio Pochettino’s debut as manager became about damage limitation from that point on.

And yet in the post-match analysis, Manchester United’s first-choice goalkeeper still found himself scrutinised. “If he’s in the right position, he saves it comfortably,” argued Danny Murphy on Match of the Day, highlighting Lammens’ positioning for Dominik Szoboszlai's opener.

“It’s a poor goalkeeping error.”.

In a recent development, it wasn’t the first time a Lammens mistake has been highlighted this season. While the Belgian was widely hailed for his performances in his debut Premier League campaign after joining from Royal Antwerp, the malaise around him at Old Trafford has dragged him down. He, like many of his United teammates, is under-performing.

It has been revealed that before the November international break, Lammens was blamed for two goals in the chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, too easily beaten at his near post by Alysson for Villa’s first and spilling a shot for Nicolas Jackson to make it 2-0 after only four minutes. He was shaky throughout.

Industry observers note that there was also Lammens’ ill-judged decision to come rushing off his line against Bournemouth, giving Evanilson the chance to finish into an empty net in a 3-0 win for the Cherries at Old Trafford. The messy own goal conceded by Manchester United in the 1-1 draw away to Fulham was another that involved Lammens.

Recent findings suggest that like so many at United right now, Lammens is clearly low on confidence. His struggles can be traced back to the World Cup where he made a blunder that led to Belgium’s exit from the tournament, spilling a shot for Mikel Merino to score a late winner for Spain. Lammens hasn’t been the same since that moment.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

There are, however, some mitigating factors to explain the goalkeeper’s form. For starters, Lammens is having to make more saves this season. Last season, the 24-year-old averaged 2.4 saves per 90 minutes in the Premier League, whereas this season that number has increased to 3.6 saves per 90 minutes.

Only Crystal Palace have conceded more Expected Goals (xG) in the Premier League this season than Manchester United. Lammens is being afforded very little protection by the players in front of him, as demonstrated by United’s shambolic defensive performance at Anfield on Sunday.

It has been revealed that for comparison, Manchester United conceded the fourth-lowest xG over the course of the 2025/26 Premier League campaign. Their sudden defensive drop-off is somewhat unexplainable, but it goes a long way to reasoning why Lammens is struggling so much. He’s simply having to do more. He’s being overwhelmed.

Lammens hasn’t actually regressed much in terms of his save percentage. This season, the Belgian is ranked 16th in the Premier League for this metric, whereas last season he was 14th. Lammens has never been anywhere near the most effective shot-stoppers in this regard.

Like so many at United right now, Lammens is clearly low on confidence.

Industry observers note that it’s possible Lammens over-performed last season. Without the Belgian settling so swiftly after arriving as an emergency upgrade on Andre Onana and Altay Bayindir, it’s difficult to envisage Manchester United finishing third. His saves did a lot to mask some of United’s structural deficiencies.

It has been revealed that no goalkeeper in the Premier League last season prevented more goals than Lammens (6.4). That ranked him ahead of the likes of Gianluigi Donnarumma, Emi Martinez, Jordan Pickford, Alisson Becker and David Raya. It was perhaps unrealistic to expect someone still so young in goalkeeper years to maintain such a high level.

Sources indicate that “This break came at the ideal moment for me,” said Lammens in the last international break during which he played the full 90 minutes in back-to-back games for Belgium against Turkey and Italy, saving a penalty against the latter. “These have been difficult weeks for me at Manchester United.”.

Life for Lammens didn’t get any easier in his first match back from international duty, although the Belgian’s seven saves prevented the scoreline from being even more humiliating for Manchester United. There were moments when Lammens showed the sort of form that made him so eye-catching last season.

Pochettino might find a way to steady Manchester United at the back. The Argentine set up the Old Trafford outfit with a back three in possession before Yoro’s red card completely changed the dynamic of the match. With 11 men on the pitch, Pochettino should find it easier to implement a defensive game plan, although that’s something Michael Carrick never managed.

This could help Lammens rediscover his best form. If not, Manchester United will need their goalkeeper to eliminate the errors from his performances on his own accord, otherwise a relegation scrap at the bottom of the Premier League table could be unavoidable. Lammens can’t count on getting any more help any time soon.

The United States will host Copa America again in 2028, soccer federations Conmebol and Concacaf confirmed Tuesday, marking its second consecutive time holding the competition.

Sources indicate that six teams from North America, Central America and the Caribbean will join 10 South American sides in the event, which runs from June 9 to July 9, 2028. Qualification for Concacaf teams will be determined through the 2027 Gold Cup.

The US hosted the last Copa America in 2024, when Argentina beat Colombia in the final. The nation also staged the competition in 2016, finishing fourth.

"After our collaboration in 2024, we are pleased to join forces again to bring the Conmebol Copa America to our region in 2028," Concacaf President Victor Montagliani said in a statement.

"This agreement will bring six Concacaf national teams a new opportunity to compete against some of the best in the world, while further reinforcing the competitive significance of our Concacaf Gold Cup.".

The federations noted that host cities and venue details will be announced at a later date.

"The Conmebol Copa America is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history, and the greatness of South American football," Conmebol President Alejandro Domínguez mentioned in a statement.

"In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with Concacaf and our shared commitment to continuing to drive the growth of football across the continent.".

According to recent reports, argentina have won the last two editions of the tournament, having also beaten Brazil 1-0 in the final back in 2021. However, they will have to defend their title without Lionel Messi in 2028 following his retirement from international football.

Messi called time on his glittering Argentina career after leading his country to the World Cup final in July, where they lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time.

He played one final friendly against Benin last month, scoring a penalty to seal a 3-0 win.

#117655. Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When world leaders agreed to do what they could to stop the world from overheating back in 2015, it was heralded as a victorious moment.
  • Since then, efforts to curb the use of planet-warming fossil fuels have achieved some success, with coal, oil and gas falling to a record low share of global primary energy supply.
  • "We're still burning stuff like [it's] the 19th century," Mark Maslin, professor of Earth System Science at University College London, told DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When world leaders agreed to do what they could to stop the world from overheating back in 2015, it was heralded as a victorious moment. Hope rippled from Paris, where the historic deal was made.

Since then, efforts to curb the use of planet-warming fossil fuels have achieved some success, with coal, oil and gas falling to a record low share of global primary energy supply. But they still account for around 86% of the world's energy.

"We're still burning stuff like [it's] the 19th century," Mark Maslin, professor of Earth System Science at University College London, told DW.

And that has consequences. The United Nations now says overshooting the temperature threshold agreed in Paris 11 years ago is inevitable. That means even more extreme weather events, like storms, flooding, droughts and deadly heat waves and resultant crop failures and water shortages across the world.

Sources indicate that the impacts are already being felt globally. This summer, Europe alone recorded 50,000 heat-related deaths in urban areas. In Delhi, India, summer heat waves saw temperatures soar above 45 degrees Celsius (113 Fahrenheit). Even in the relative cool of the evening, there was little respite.

Sources indicate that "It feels like your eyes are burning," remarked Disha Ravi, co-founder of the India chapter of youth climate movement Fridays for Future (FFF). "I always describe it as being cooked alive in an oven.".

Heat waves and other weather extremes are killing people now, claims Ravi, and she is aware that as the global average temperature continues to rise, life is only set to become tougher.

"Even at this moment where we haven't even reached the worst of what it could be, it's already difficult," she said.

"We should have dealt with climate change 10, 20 years ago," Maslin noted.

The UN now says that the world must keep the time it spends in overshoot as brief as possible, bringing global heating back down by the end of the century.

The longer the planet spends above the threshold, the greater the risk of triggering irreversible, self-perpetuating tipping points, such as massive forest die-back and permafrost melting that would release huge amounts of carbon into the atmosphere.

A recent report by science-based assessment Climate Action Tracker says limiting overshoot will require policies to rapidly and steeply reduce the emissions warping the climate.

"The stark choice for governments is to continue to support the fossil fuel industry, which would consign humanity to insurmountable economic damages, rising mortality from heat and climate-driven diseases and disasters that they are unable to adapt to — or pivot to the solutions which are available and cheaper than ever," the authors said.

Failure to cut emissions rapidly has made it significantly harder to get climate change under control, and the window for doing so is rapidly closing. But Maslin refers to a Chinese proverb: "When is the best time to plant a tree? Yesterday. When's the next best time to plant a tree? Today.".

He points to the massive expansion in renewable energy as reason not to despair. Wind, solar and hydropower accounted for around 34% of global electricity production in 2025 and are increasingly being used to meet rising demand.

Last year, record growth in solar power meant that clean energy met all fresh global electricity demand, stifling new fossil fuel generation, according to an analysis by energy think tank Ember.

"At the moment, $2 trillion is being invested in new renewable energy projects around the world, which is twice as much as fossil fuels," Maslin remarked.

But no country is weaning itself off fossil fuels quickly enough to limit the time spent in overshoot. "The transition is happening, it's just not happening fast enough," he added.

One of the problems is that most climate and energy aims focus on building a green energy system rather than creating policy to shift away from fossil fuel use and production, according to a recent report on how to manage the transition by nonprofit research organization, World Resources Institute.

A group of 57 states is working together to manage and accelerate the complicated task of phasing out oil, coal and gas by creating specific roadmaps to do so.

Under the Transition Away from Fossil Fuels initiative (TAFF) initiative, Brazil has published a global roadmap that suggests various measures that can be tailored to each country's financial circumstances and capabilities.

So far, a small but growing number of countries, including Ireland, Denmark, the Netherlands, France, Germany, and Finland, have released national roadmaps.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Yet renewables advocacy group Oil Change International says they largely repackage existing commitments rather than offering new ones, when "what we need is an accelerated timeline for a clean, secure energy system.".

Industry observers note that france is sticking to a previously confirmed deadline of phasing out fossil fuels entirely by 2050. The Netherlands has not published binding dates for quitting oil and gas, and will continue to extract gas in the North Sea.

Germany, however, explicitly mentioned transitioning away from fossil fuels by 2045 for the first time, in line with its existing climate neutrality target. The country has also reduced its emissions by 48% compared to 1990 levels.

And while Finland has not set a hard and fast target for phasing out the fossil fuels that still account for 26% of its total energy consumption, it already generates more than 96% of electricity from non-fossil sources.

"None of these examples is a perfect template," according to the WRI report. "But together, they show that countries are already developing many of the core ingredients of a fossil fuel transition blueprint.".

Limiting the time spent in overshoot would mean fossil fuel use falling 20% by 2030 and being phased out completely by 2070, according to research institute Climate Analytics.

It also means removing hundreds of billions of tons of CO2 from the atmosphere using carbon removal technologies that remain unproven at scale, as well as nature-based approaches like reforestation.

And it requires fast action on the short-lived but highly potent greenhouse gas methane. A 45% cut would reduce warming by 0.3%, according to the UN.

Scientists stress that every fraction of a degree matters as the world blows past the threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) of warming above pre-industrial levels. That's because every increment will bring more extreme heat, heavier rainfall, rising seas, and greater and more catastrophic risk for everyone around the world.

Still, even in the face of accelerating climate change, FFF co-founder Ravi rejects the idea that it is too late to act.

It has been revealed that "I refuse to believe we'll ever run out of time. No matter how bad it gets," she said. "We owe it to ourselves. We owe it to each other to always try to get out of this mess.".

Just eight universities dominate Nobel and other top economics prizes

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1154 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers from Harvard and seven other US universities including MIT, Princeton and Yale, dominate economics prizes.Credit: Jade Gao/AFP via Getty.
  • Major prizes in economics, including the Nobel are being awarded to researchers affiliated to an increasingly concentrated set of US universities, according to a working paper published last month1.
  • Eight institutions dominate the world's top economics prizes, led Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers from Harvard and seven other US universities including MIT, Princeton and Yale, dominate economics prizes.Credit: Jade Gao/AFP via Getty.

Major prizes in economics, including the Nobel are being awarded to researchers affiliated to an increasingly concentrated set of US universities, according to a working paper published last month1.

Eight institutions dominate the world's top economics prizes, led Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Recent findings suggest that this contrasts with prizes awarded in disciplines in the natural sciences, engineering and social sciences outside economics. These have become less concentrated among certain instituions over the past 70 years, according to the working paper, which has not yet been peer reviewed.

“The whole world now does science,” notes Richard Freeman, an economist at Harvard University and an author on the paper, which is an enhancement to an article presented at a National Bureau of Economic Research Summer Institute workshop in a 20242. “Our initial thought was that as the science spreads out, so too should all the prizes.” And that was the case — except in economics where “it went the other direction”.

Economist John Hassler, who is based at Stockholm University and chairs the prize-awarding committee for the Economics Prize in Memory of Alfred Nobel, says that the overall finding of concentration among a small group of US universities is not a complete surprise.

It has been revealed that “The trend is truly eye-opening and adds another dimension to the understanding of inequality within the economics profession,” adds Ashwini Deshpande, an economist at Ashoka University in Sonipat, India. “The low levels of gender, ethnic and geographic diversity within authors of top journal papers and prizes is well known and a matter of concern.”.

Freeman and his colleagues examined 171 different awards and focused their analyses on those given between 1960 and 2022, including Nobel prizes (except for literature and peace), the Fields Medal for mathematics and the Breakthrough science prizes established in 2012 by the founders of technology companies among others.

It has been revealed that the authors of the working paper analysed the academic affiliations of the 5,859 prizewinners, working out the number of years they were linked to a specific institution. They call this metric ‘affiliation years’.

According to recent reports, of the 18 scientific fields of the prizewinners, 17 had a greater variety of universities represented among recipients over the time period. Economics was the outlier.

Industry observers note that among winners of the economics Nobel prize, seven out of 148 institutions made up 50% of affiliation years. It means that, of all the years that economics Nobel prizewinners dedicated to their discipline in academia, half of them were spent in the seven institutions.

Sources indicate that for chemistry Nobels, 23 institutions out of 216 accounted for half of affiliation years. Twenty-six out of 243 institutions accounted for 50% of affiliation years for the physiology or medicine Nobel, and 17 out of 200 for the physics prize.

It has been revealed that when the authors assessed all the main economics prizes between 1960 and 2022 (not only the Nobel), they found that researchers from eight out of 249 institutions represented 50% of affiliation years. In addition to Harvard, the eight are: the University of Chicago in Illinois; Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in Cambridge; Stanford University in California; Princeton University in Fresh Jersey; Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut; the University of California, Berkeley; and Columbia University in New York.

By contrast, for assessed prizes in the natural sciences, 37 institutions out of 1,318 account for 50% of affiliation-years as of 2022; for engineering prizes it is 27 out of 783; and for social sciences prizes (minus economics), it is 23 out of 744. Unlike in economics, the trend for these fields is towards less concentration (see ‘Spot the outlier’).

Sources indicate that the authors propose some possible explanations. One of these relates to another finding of the paper: “The institutions producing most of the field’s recognized work also establish the toolkit that the rest of the fields adopts,” the paper’s authors say. “Work using an unfamiliar approach is hard to place or recognize, and findings that disagree with the main tenets of the field are rejected rather than studied as special cases that may yield upcoming knowledge.”.

According to recent reports, another factor, they report is that in economics, 55 per cent of Nobel laureates received the prize for a broad body of work. This contrasts somewhat with medicine and the other sciences. Some 50 per cent of prize winners in chemistry, 59 per cent in physics and 70 per cent in medicine were awarded for testable findings.

Hanzhang Zhou, a co-author on the paper and an economics doctoral candidate at MIT, notes: “When you’re giving the prize for somebody’s lifetime agenda, the institution that they’re associated with is usually one of the factors that you do take into account,” she explains.

It has been revealed that hassler told Nature that the economics prize is not intended to be a lifetime achievement award and follows the rules governing the other prize categories. He indicates it is a prize for a well-defined contribution or breakthrough, should also lead to further research in the field and that the finding must also have relevance to society at large.

Morocco FA filed challenge against Cas arbitrator less than hour before Afcon final verdict

  • Senegal contested the Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions after the team staged an injury-time walk-off in protest to a penalty awarded against them, and were successful in their appeal as Cas, sport’s highest court, found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law” when he decided to resume the match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Morocco’s federation submitted a last-minute challenge to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) against a member of the judicial panel before Senegal saw their Africa Cup of Nations appeal upheld, restoring them as 2025 champions.

Senegal contested the Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions after the team staged an injury-time walk-off in protest to a penalty awarded against them, and were successful in their appeal as Cas, sport’s highest court, found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law” when he decided to resume the match.

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) responded to Tuesday’s verdict by questioning “the integrity and credibility of the arbitration process”, a complaint surrounding an alleged phone call involving Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) president Abdoulaye Fall and arbitrator Ulrich Haas.

The Independent understands that Cas received a challenge against Haas by the FRMF within one hour prior to the decision being unveiled. This formally came several hours after media reports stated it had already been filed.

The Icas Challenge Commission reviewed the FRMF’s challenge but found there was not enough evidence at the time to delay the verdict’s announcement.

Sources indicate that Haas strongly denies any direct contact at any moment with the Senegalese federation or any parties involved throughout the arbitration process, while the FSF also vehemently refuted the allegations as “fake news”.

The FRMF has vowed to pursue further legal action to appeal the verdict.

A statement read: “The Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (Ifab) and Fifa, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

“Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kelly Somers has recalled a deeply personal moment with Sir Gareth Southgate after England’s victory over Germany at Euro 2020 – and a thoughtful gesture the former Three Lions manager made when she was pregnant.

Sir Gareth's England beat Germany 2-0 at Wembley in June 2021, 25 years after his decisive penalty miss against the same opponents in the Euro 96 semi-finals, and the result prompted an emotional reflection on the team-mates he felt he had let down all those years ago.

As the BBC’s England reporter, Somers was there to capture that reaction, and says it remains one of the standout conversations of her time following the national side.

Asked for her favourite interviews over her years covering England, Somers told FourFourTwo: “[Southgate] said he’d looked up to the significant screen midway through the game and seen David Seaman sitting there.

Industry observers note that “He mentioned 'I know I can never undo any of the heartache I caused them, but hopefully this has gone a long way'. Hearing him say that was really special.”.

Somers was also touched by an off-camera gesture delivered by Southgate during her pregnancy in 2023.

She remarked: “When I was pregnant in 2023, Gareth gave me a little England kit for my daughter in a gift bag.”.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“In true Gareth Southgate fashion, he said 'I didn’t actually know about your pregnancy, my team arranged this, but this is on behalf of the FA'.

"He didn’t want to take the credit for it, which I thought was lovely.”.

Somers also picked out interviewing Ollie Watkins dramatic winner against the Netherlands in the Euro 2024 semi-final as a highlight.

She mentioned: "It felt like I was talking to a boy from the park, I was speaking to someone at pretty much the pinnacle of their life.

In a recent development, “There was another where I had to wait for Jude Bellingham after a drugs test, and he came out in just his top and pants. I thought ‘This is all very weird!’ But he’s always very good in interviews.".

Somers added: "To be the in-camp reporter is incredible, because pretty much every day you get 15 minutes with a different player, so I’ve got to know them. I love interviewing and the challenge of bringing out the human side of players.

"At the Euros in 2021, I did one with Jack Grealish where he spoke about his sister – he’s incredibly close to his family. When the interview ended, he said “I was getting emotional, I didn’t expect that.”.

Senegal re-crowned Afcon champions after appeal upheld

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • Senegal have been re-crowned the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) unanimously upheld their appeal against the decision to strip them of their title on Tuesday.
  • Senegal contested Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions, which wiped the Teranga Lions’ title from the records despite victory in January’s Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Senegal have been re-crowned the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) unanimously upheld their appeal against the decision to strip them of their title on Tuesday.

Senegal contested Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions, which wiped the Teranga Lions’ title from the records despite victory in January’s Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat.

The final was fraught with controversy after Senegal staged a walk-off in protest to a penalty was awarded against them in the dying stages of normal time, with players ordered into the dressing room by manager Pape Thiaw, where they remained for 14 minutes.

It has been revealed that play was eventually resumed before Morocco’s Brahim Diaz missed the spot-kick, sailing a tame ‘Panenka’ effort into the arms of Edouard Mendy. Senegal went on to win the match in extra time through Pape Gueye.

However, they were stripped of the title two months later after Caf’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited ⁠the match by walking off the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 ​victory to ⁠Morocco.

Senegal rapidly followed with an appeal to sport's highest court, Cas, which was lodged on 25 March and have now successfully fought their case to be reinstated as champions, with the original 1-0 result restored.

The three-man Cas ‌panel, presided over by French sports law ​expert Gerald Simon with assistance from ‌Italian international law professor ⁠Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based ⁠attorney Ulrich Haas, ‌unanimously found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law”, noted Cas secretary general Matthieu Reeb.

Ndala’s decision to resume the match after Senegal’s walk-off fell within his sole authority and was therefore covered by the “field of play” doctrine, something Morocco’s federation argued was not the case.

The court published its reasoning in a press release issued on Tuesday afternoon, which read: “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

“In the panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.”.

The panel clarified that Articles 82 and 84 of Caf’s tournament regulations, cited in the Moroccan federation’s appeal, apply only to determining match results if team conduct forces a referee to permanently call off a game, and were therefore not applicable in this instance.

"In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law," a court press release added.

It has been revealed that “The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary'. On the contrary, the referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.".

Cas noted that disciplinary action has already been taken against then-Senegal boss Thiaw, the Senegalese federation and certain players following separate proceedings by Caf.

Senegal took to social media to celebrate the verdict, posting a picture of the team lifting the trophy with the caption, “Encore et toujours champions d’Afrique” - which translates to, “Champions of Africa, once again and always”.

“The Senegalese Football Federation welcomes this sentence with deep satisfaction,” a federation statement read.

“Far from consecrating the preeminence of one party over another, this decision affirms above all the triumph of sporting fairness and recalls a cardinal principle: the truth of a match is established exclusively on the field, under the protection of sports law.

“On this solemn occasion, the FSF wishes to express its deep gratitude to the Lions of Teranga and their management, to its lawyers and advisors, to the President of the Republic and the Senegalese Government for their support, as well as to all supporters, both in Senegal and in the diaspora.”.

The Moroccan federation (FRMF) released a statement confirming its intention to “pursue all available legal avenues” to appeal the decision.

The federation alleged there had been “communication” between a member of the Cas panel and the president of the Senegalese federation 48 hours before the decision was issued.

The FRMF stated these practices would “compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure”.

Cas has been contacted for comment regarding this allegation.

The FRMF added that the decision “did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and Fifa, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties”.

Cas initially promised a decision within days of the 8 October in-person hearing in Lausanne but then decided to issue a complete ruling, including legal grounds, known as a Cas Award - a process that requires several weeks.

Cas Awards hold the same value as a national court judgement, enforceable in accordance with the Fresh York Convention on the Recognition ‌and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards.

The full Cas Award will be published in due course.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany's flagship airline Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, according to a manufacturer letter seen by German news agency DPA and news outlets.

The letter was reportedly signed by Lufthansa CEO Jens Ritter and four other board members.

Recent findings suggest that this is reportedly down to ongoing financial losses. In the first nine months of the year, the airline recorded an operating loss of €180 million ($197 million).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The executive board said on average the loss amounts to €20 million every month, according to media reports. The board stated in the letter that "this is the third year in a row of not being financially successful.".

"Lufthansa is presently not competitive in terms of its cost structure, efficiency and productivity," the letter said.

At the end of 2025, the Lufthansa group employed some 67,100 people, up 1% from the previous year.

The tech giant also plans to cut employee travel benefits, restructure its hub operations to reduce crew overnight stays abroad, and reduce short- and medium-haul capacity by replacing some A320 aircraft with A220 jets.

Recent findings suggest that furthermore, it plans to equip ten aircraft per month with Starlink, a satellite internet service developed by tech billionaire Elon Musk. The airline hopes to generate "additional revenue” by monetizing onboard internet access, according to the letter.

Recent findings suggest that the time frame of the cuts is unclear. It's also unknown whether the cuts were a part of a previously unveiled downsizing.

In September 2025, Lufthansa remarked it would slash 4,000 administrative positions due to the implementation of AI and digitalization.

In regards to this year, Lufthansa has faced rising fuel costs spurred by the US-Israeli war with Iran, further complicating its financial outlook.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.

Industry observers note that there were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came. Even in the 95th minute, Arteta’s players were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League game might have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. By half-time it should have been a formality. Yet, as chance after chance slipped away, there was always a possibility this would end differently.

Industry observers note that the leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived. Even so, they did just that and, liberated in the second half, Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser in his team’s best period. There were still 40 minutes for Arsenal to put this one to bed and they found many ways not to do so.

It was notable that the man who put Arsenal ahead in the ninth minute with a right-footed thump from space on the edge of the Dortmund box was the same striker who would miss the best chance to win it. That is the Viktor Gyökeres dilemma. In the space of a single game he can look like a potential match-winner and also the last man his manager would wish to see arriving on the end of a perfect Martin Odegaard cross.

According to recent reports, so it proved after 75 minutes when Gyökeres thrust himself at an Odegaard ball into the box that just needed guiding inside a post, yet planted it decisively wide of the mark. On the touchline Arteta tried very hard to hide his despair and failed to do so.

It ended that way, with a heroic defensive performance from the Dortmund defence, including one memorable moment when substitute Serhou Guirassy’s determination to block a cross prompted a double ricochet off his own post. One could make the argument that there were times when it was “unbelievable”, as Arteta later said, that the ball did not find its way in. Although there were also moments when the reasons were self-evident.

“There’s an element of luck,” the Arsenal manager mentioned, “and there is an element of us [not] finishing better.”.

According to recent reports, in fifth place in the league phase table, dropped points at home do not carry the same jeopardy in the group stage that they once did, yet even so there was a truth for Arteta to chew upon. This is a well-honed, substantial-game Arsenal Champions League side that he has built. One that reached the final last season and may well go close again, but as ever they seem to be doing so in spite of the great goalscorer that so many of their nearest rivals have at their disposal.

Arteta sounded that warning after defeat in the final in Budapest at the end of May and, while changes have been made, it would be hard to argue that they have been fundamental. This was a good opponent – the leaders of the Bundesliga with many exports from English football who have been reconditioned for the German game. Those include Fábio Silva, Felix Nmecha and Jobe Bellingham, who had a second-half goal narrowly disallowed for offside.

In defence their captain Nico Schlotterbeck and Waldemar Anton will not have many better games. They might have been fortunate at times but they will also point to a penalty that was not given, when Gyökeres handled in his own area at the start of the second half.

Industry observers note that gyökeres’s first-half goal was certainly among the best he has scored for the club, invited to shoot by a Dortmund defence that simply stood off as he reached the edge of the area. He will not catch many as full as he did this one. More of a dig than a swish but with the useful consequence of packing a lot of power and a dip that meant goalkeeper Gregor Kobel saw it but could not pick out its flight.

It has been revealed that even so, there was some of the Gyökeres the Arsenal manager does not need as early as the end of the first half when he launched a wild shot over from Noni Madueke’s pass. That came after Beier’s equaliser when Dortmund were at their counter-attacking best. In the final stages, Arsenal pressed hard for the winner and, although there were lots of shots, it would be hard to say there were lots of chances. The one that got away was the one that fell to Gyökeres.

Arteta would later call it “a brilliant performance”. It was hard to shake the feeling from some of the caveats he added that, like everyone else, what he really thought – above all – was that his team should have won.

The performance was superb and there is no question about that from the start to the end. We played against a really good side and the domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more.

I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.

It has been revealed that that’s what we want [to finish in the top eight]. We have a big game against Manchester City at home on Sunday so we need to recover really well, we have four days to do that and sustain that momentum the way we are playing and the win will come.

We’re champions, we’re at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates. There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction.

I feel like the performances from us up until the last shot was incredible at times. Definitely feels like two points dropped like the other day so, having dominated so much of the game we need to take all the points.

Recent findings suggest that I prefer this type of game [more open rather than against a deep defence], there are more breaks and opportunities to attack space. We it’s a low block it’s more about pass, pass, pass and wait for the right moment. I feel like we are well-suited to both types of game.

According to recent reports, from the second phase of the next corner, Tzolis volleyed miles over when a shot was not on.
