Windsor Park would require 5,000 additional seats to host games at the 2035 World Cup.

The Irish Football Association's director of women's football Angela Platt stated the organisation is "still working through" intends with the Northern Ireland government to ensure there is funding available to make the necessary upgrades to Windsor Park in time for the 2035 World Cup.

It was confirmed on Monday that Northern Ireland, England, Scotland and Wales, the only bidders for the tournament in nine years' time, had been ratified as co-hosts.

Of the 19 venues proposed by the 'All Together' bid, Belfast's Windsor Park is the sole stadium in Northern Ireland, but would require an additional 5,000 seats to its current capacity of 18,500 as well as changes to the pitch and floodlights.

"We're obviously working with our government partners who've committed their support to help us do that, and we'll continue our endeavours to make sure that we work towards that," Platt told BBC NI's Stephen Watson.

"We know that the Northern Ireland Executive has given a commitment to back us and do whatever they can to support us in our endeavours to make sure we're ready for that hosting of the Women's World Cup in 2035.

"We have a few years to make sure we work through that.".

Northern Ireland was involved in a similar bid to host games at Euro 2028, but looks for fixtures in Belfast at that tournament fell through when the government mentioned it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in the required timescale.

Platt stated that "was in the past" and that the organisation were focused on the work required to avoid any repeat.

Sources indicate that "We're still working towards making sure that it does happen and we're positive. We know that the work is there to make sure that it happens," she added.

"It's obviously disappointing when something that people work so hard to put together doesn't come to fruition, but certainly that's in the past for us.

"From our perspective, working for women's football, this is a great opportunity for Northern Ireland to get behind this and actually make sure that we do everything we can to host our Women's World Cup games here.".

UK to host 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa confirms.

Plans to increase Windsor Park capacity to 23,750.

There is no guarantee that, even as co-hosts, there would an automatic qualification spot for Northern Ireland.

The side last qualified for a major tournament at Euro 2022 and Platt believes bringing the World Cup to the country has the potential to "inspire a new generation".

Sources indicate that "I think it can have a huge impact. We've always been blessed that we have had our women's team involved in the Women's Euros in 2022, and through my role, I get to visit other nations hosting tournaments such as this," she stated.

"I was in Sydney for the Women's World Cup (2023) and obviously saw the impact hosting a tournament like that had in Newly introduced Zealand and Australia, and likewise for the Euros in England and Switzerland recently.

Sources indicate that "That impact is significant. It's the growth of the game, it's the engagement, it's the legacy. So much positivity can come out of hosting major tournaments and we're excited to play our part in this and it can only have benefits for Northern Ireland in general.".

Bruno Fernandes was devastated Michael Carrick was sacked as Manchester United manager, according to his former teammate Rasmus Hojlund.

The Napoli striker, who completed his £44m move away from Old Trafford in the summer, is convinced that his old team, who are 19th in the Premier League, will only have a temporary stay in the relegation zone.

And Hojlund, a boyhood United fan who joined them for £64m in 2023, believes they have too much quality to go down.

The Denmark international was back in Manchester to score for Napoli against City in Tuesday’s 2-2 draw in the Champions League.

It has been revealed that and he said: “I am watching all the games I can, especially from the red side of Manchester. It is unfortunate [that United are struggling].”.

United have not won in their last nine league games, dating back to August, and lost 4-0 to Liverpool on Sunday in Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge.

They are second from bottom but Hojlund is not worried. “It is a temporary picture, I think they will get back to the top, the Premier League is like this,” he mentioned. “I read the other day that Bournemouth were in the relegation zone after a couple of games, now they have won the last five games and are in the top half of the table.

According to recent reports, “They have got a lot of quality, I have seen the guys training day by day and I know the players really well and they have got a great squad, good leaders, good professionals so I am sure they will turn it around. Hopefully they will get it right with Mauricio.”.

Captain Fernandes was dropped by Carrick after questioning his tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como but he and Diogo Dalot caught up with Hojlund when Denmark faced Portugal and the forward stated they were upset the manager was losing his job.

“In the international break when I spoke with Bruno and Diogo, they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going but also looking forward to some change,” Hojlund added. “I am still speaking with Patrick [Dorgu, his Denmark teammate] and I just wish the guys all the best and I am sure they will turn it around this season.”.

Hojlund, who scored 26 goals in 95 games in two seasons at Old Trafford, noted playing for United comes with great pressure, making it harder in the bad times.

“United is a massive club and you can’t take anything away from that,” he mentioned. “There are so many people following the club around the world and you can’t really escape from it, it is almost too high when it is good and almost too low when it is bad so it is all about trying to be in that middle and now I think I tried both the highs and the lows there. The pressure is part of the club. It comes with playing for Man United.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kansas City Current, who were formed in 2020, won this year's National Women's Soccer League championship.

"It's turning into our Super Bowl moment.".

Sarah Jones Simmer, chief operating officer of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL), could not wait for the championship game between Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current on Saturday night.

The NWSL showpiece was played out in front of a sellout crowd of more than 19,000 at Audi Field in Washington DC, with tickets retailing at more than $300 (Â£229).

Ultimately, the Current triumphed 2-1 to clinch their first title, condemning Spirit to an unwanted record of three lost finals in a row.

Just a few hours earlier on this side of the Atlantic, Alexia Putellas, who last month was crowned the best player in the world for the third time at the Ballon d'Or ceremony, was scoring twice for London City against Crystal Palace in front of 4,000 people in Bromley.

It is a totally unfair comparison. After all, a championship final is the type of jamboree the USA does particularly well.

Nevertheless, women's football is booming in America at the moment, with attendance figures at record highs, more franchises joining the league and club retail sales double those of 2025.

So what is behind the explosion in popularity?

And what can the Women's Super League learn from it?

The US is the most successful nation in women's international football.

The four-time World Cup winners (1991, 1999, 2015 and 2019) and five-time Olympic gold medallists, the nation of Mia Hamm, Alex Morgan and Megan Rapinoe, has a history of winning - and the domestic game is key.

"If anything, soccer is more seen as a women's sport [in the USA]," states broadcaster Jacqui Oatley, who at the moment commentates on the NWSL for ESPN.

"Women have won World Cups and Olympic Games - and the men have been nowhere near as successful.".

While teams in the United States became professional in 2001 - for WSL teams it was 2018 - the top flight has taken several different guises over the years.

The current NWSL kicked off in 2013 as an eight-team competition, and has since expanded to 16 franchises, with two more joining from 2028.

There is no relegation and Kansas City's victory on Saturday means the league has had eight different winners since its iteration.

As the below graph shows, the ownership picture for these sides is far more varied than in the UK, with American sides much less dependent on their male counterparts.

It has been revealed that indeed, Kansas City are blazing a trail. Established in December 2020, unaffiliated to a men's side and backed by ambitious owners that include Brittany Mahomes - the wife of NFL quarterback Patrick Mahomes.

It has been revealed that winning the championship is the crowning achievement for an ambitious franchise and such success is something independent London City hope to emulate in the UK. They are four points from the WSL summit nearly halfway through the 2026-27 season.

Industry observers note that kansas City were also the first club to build a bespoke stadium solely for women's football and the demand for seats at their 11,500-seater CPKC Stadium is huge. Earlier this year, Brighton announced their own purpose-built venue, planned for 2030-31.

"I think our independence is a hallmark of the league," says the NWSL's Jones Simmer.

"It is something we are very proud of. It allows us to invest in our own growth, prioritise the women's game and ensure resources are flowing to it.".

It is markedly different from the UK set-up, where all WSL teams bar London City are, at least, affiliated and more often financially reliant on the men's side.

But that presents just as much of an opportunity, according to Jones Simmer.

"I know Nikki [Doucet, chief executive of the WSL] and I admire what she is building," she claims.

"There's a really unique opportunity to build on the legacy of these 100-year-old men's clubs that are household names, to build women's brands that embrace the legacy but also have their own identity.".

Bespoke women's football stadiums? Why US sides are making the move.

Brighton plan Europe's first purpose-built Â£80m women's stadium.

Washington Spirit's Trinity Rodman benefited from a NWSL decision in December 2025 to lift the league's salary cap for a 'High Impact Player'.

Fans of both the NWSL and the WSL are spoiled when it comes to talent.

Most of the US national team play their club football at home, with the likes of Trinity Rodman, Mallory Swanson and Rose Lavelle household names.

International stars such as Malawi's Temwa Chawinga at Kansas City, who came 10th in the 2026 Ballon d'Or rankings, and former Chelsea striker Sam Kerr further enhance the league's quality.

Industry observers note that "Where it starts is the product on the pitch," states Jones Simmer. "The quality of football has to be incredible and we have the best players in the world.

Recent findings suggest that "And they are incredibly engaging with our fans. For so many supporters, their entry point to the league is they care about a particular player.".

Provided the standard of competition is present, Jones Simmer claims fans will return - and her confidence is backed up by the numbers.

In 2026, the average gate for an NWSL match has been more than 11,000 - only Arsenal in the WSL consistently receive a higher attendance than that, albeit the US is almost five times more populous than the UK.

On Thursday, the final few tickets for the NWSL's showpiece were retailing at $300 on ticket site Viagogo, with Jones Simmer suggesting resale tickets could be purchased at six times market value in advance of the match.

As London City and Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang put it: "The answer could not be clearer that there is an audience for the women's game.".

"It's our job to hook fans by making sure they have a great experience watching a game in a venue and that's about the quality of the product," Jones Simmer adds.

"Once folks have that experience, it's a really easy yes to tune in again.".

Families v loyal fans - women's football's attendance dilemma.

Not that quality is an issue in the WSL where high-class footballers abound. Take Putellas, goal machine Khadija Shaw and most of England's double European Championship-winning squad for example.

American stars such as Alyssa Thompson and Naomi Girma at Chelsea, and Manchester City's Sam Coffey, have also swapped the US for the WSL in the past two years.

Broadcaster Oatley, who has been covering women's football since the 2005 World Cup, is keen for such players to be more visible off the pitch.

"I would love to see WSL players on mainstream TV shows, podcasts, social media platforms, not just on women's football programmes where the audience already knows everything about them," she says.

"It would not be for everyone, but for those who are comfortable, who have the biggest personalities, I think we could use that much more to grow our audience.".

Oatley has been covering NWSL games for the past four seasons and she believes US clubs have mastered putting on events.

"When you're trying to promote a product in sport, you can't guarantee the team is going to play well and win," she indicates.

"But you can ensure the people who come to the game have a great experience.

"I love the enthusiasm, the positivity, the vibe of 'let's make this massive'. It's a brilliant experience.".

According to recent reports, it is a balance the WSL wrestles with. With attendances plateauing this season, questions have arisen around its target audience and whether to market matches such as the north London derby between Tottenham and Arsenal as a rivalry or a family-friendly event.

Oatley's perspective is that it ought to be both, while recognising the different challenges in this country.

Industry observers note that "I didn't understand that criticism," she says, "because they weren't saying: 'Only come to this game if you're a family'. It was being promoted all round.

"I don't think it's one size fits all marketing wise - the main thing is awareness.".

The NWSL Fan Fest at The Wharf in Washington DC was part of a series of events around the championship game on Saturday.

It is a challenge the NWSL has embraced, and seen attendances rise accordingly.

"We want to ensure that we provided a big enough tent where everyone can feel welcome and included, whether they're there for the rivalries and the competitive tactics, or they're experiencing it for the first time," states Jones Simmer.

"To grow the sport, all fans need to be able to come to an NWSL game and have a great experience.".

This season, league finalists Current and Spirit played at a remarkable 17 different times between them, reflecting the four timezones and vast nature of the USA.

It is all part of the country's sporting landscape, but given the WSL's continued conundrum about fixture scheduling, it is interesting that NWSL supporters manage to find the matches regardless.

"I have a lot of sympathy with schedulers because men's football got there first," Oatley says.

"Maybe the solution is deciding certain time slots are for women's football and sticking with them.".

It does not appear the growth in the NWSL will slow down any time soon.

The Women's World Cup in Brazil next summer will feature the USA as one of the favourites and women's soccer will feature at the Olympic Games in Los Angeles in 2028.

The US will also host the 2031 Women's World Cup.

"It is amazing how the NWSL is cracking into culture," Jones Simmer says.

"We get excited about these catalytic opportunities to expand the community engagement, awareness and relevance of the NWSL.".

Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1048 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it is becoming increasingly difficult for young people in Germany to find a job after finishing university or professional training.
  • Furthermore, young people do not feel that politicians are taking action on issues that matter to them, such as climate protection.
  • Sources indicate that what particularly infuriates many young people is being talked about rather than spoken to.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it is becoming increasingly difficult for young people in Germany to find a job after finishing university or professional training. And finding an affordable place to live in a significant city, and finally starting to live independently is becoming almost impossible.

Furthermore, young people do not feel that politicians are taking action on issues that matter to them, such as climate protection. The climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, is a case in point. It, therefore, shouldn't be a surprise that young people across Europe once again took to the streets this Friday, which was World Children's Day too, to make their voices heard. In Germany, Gen Z protests took place in 73 towns and cities.

Sources indicate that what particularly infuriates many young people is being talked about rather than spoken to. Equally infuriating is seeing their protests branded as criminal before they have even begun, all because of the actions of a small minority.

One example of such rhetoric was when the youth wing of the conservative Christian Democratic Union/Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) party in Berlin-Mitte suggested deploying the German army against demonstrations.

It can also be seen in the media, such as when Bild, Germany's highest-circulation tabloid, ran a headline that translated as: "Young, male, known to the police — who rioted after the demonstrations and where chaos threatens today.".

"Young people are taking to the streets because they feel they are not being heard. And, of course, that feeling is strongly reinforced when the press devotes no more than a brief paragraph to their demands while focusing the rest of its coverage on how these protests could become problematic," states Erik Sczygiol, who until recently was deputy secretary-general of the Federal Conference of Student Representatives. "Of course, any potential security concerns need to be addressed, but they should not overshadow media coverage of the protests.".

Sources indicate that the 18-year-old Sczygiol is almost an exception. He was invited to participate in the launch of the World Population Report in Bonn alongside representatives of the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and the German Foundation for World Population (DSW). This year's report, entitled "Succeeding Generations: Empowering young people to chart the future," is particularly noteworthy because it focuses on Gen Z.

Sources indicate that UN researchers surveyed 109,000 people across 73 countries for the report, some of whose findings are encouraging. Young people worldwide are better educated than any generation before them, with 78% of adolescents across the globe completing at least lower secondary education. But finding a job is becoming increasingly difficult, while informal employment is on the rise.

This economic uncertainty has far-reaching consequences for young people. According to the report, people often do not achieve financial independence until they are in their mid-to-late 20s, and a stable partnership and parenthood are often not realities before their early-to-mid 30s.

Industry observers note that nor do young people have a seat at the political decision-making table when it comes to shaping future reforms in the labor market, housing or climate protection. Florian Brod, 25, points out: "Almost half of the world's population is under 30, yet only 2.6% of parliamentarians worldwide are under 30.".

Young people need and want change to protect their livelihoods and those of future generations. "Yet those who will have to live longest with the consequences of today's decisions are precisely the ones who have hardly any representation in the political decision-making process," claims Brod.

It has been revealed that he is somewhat close to the political decision-making process as he has served as a Youth Delegate for Sustainable Development for almost two years. In this role, he represents the interests of young people in Germany at United Nations conferences. This is certainly an crucial step towards giving his generation a greater say in political processes.

According to recent reports, nevertheless, both Brod and Sczygiol have had similar experiences. They often participate in conferences and panel discussions and are invited to submit their opinions, but these invitations often amount to little more than symbolic gestures.

"Having access to an international conference is a first step. But without substantive briefings ahead of the conference, without involvement in preliminary negotiations and, in some cases, without access to negotiation texts, there is little opportunity for us to help shape the outcome. When young people see their demands making little headway politically while they are simultaneously excluded from the search for solutions, frustration inevitably builds," indicates Brod.

Sczygiol adds: "We often get the feeling at the Federal Youth Conference that we were invited simply to provide a nice photo opportunity. We may be sitting at the table, but often only once a bill has already gone through 17 different drafts and is just days away from its final vote in the Bundestag. By that stage, young people have virtually no say in changing anything, and their voices are barely heard. Their contributions are often simply dismissed with: 'Well, that's just typical youthful nonsense.' And that is something that really frustrates young people.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Medical student Amelie Belosevic knows that feeling all too well. She served as Germany's Youth Delegate at the World Health Assembly in Geneva in May. Twenty-five countries sent youth representatives, which Belosevic sees as a clear step forward. However, she has one criticism. According to the United Nations Population Fund, 90% of the world's 1.8 billion young people live in the Global South. Yet, the region was represented by only eight delegates. As a result, Africa, Latin America and large parts of Asia were left virtually voiceless.

Her demands for Germany include better job prospects for young people entering the workforce and sustainable pension systems 40 years from now. "For a very long time, people have said 'I believe my children will have a better life than I do.' But that is no longer necessarily true. So it makes sense then that those who feel the greatest anxiety about the future are the people who have most of their life ahead of them. Sometimes, people don't understand that. We young people need to be able to believe in our future again!".

This article was originally published in German.

2023 March Madness: Will UConn or San Diego State triumph in the national championship game that 'means everything?'

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The University of Connecticut won its fifth men’s basketball national title with a 76-59 victory over San Diego State University on Monday night at NRG Stadium in Houston.
  • Senior guard Tristen Newton led UConn (31-8) with 19 points and 10 rebounds while Final Four Most Outstanding Player Adama Sanogo, a junior forward, chipped in with 17 points and 10 rebounds.
  • It has been revealed that “We weren’t ranked going into the year so we had the chip on our shoulder,” UConn head coach Dan Hurley told game broadcaster CBS.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The University of Connecticut won its fifth men’s basketball national title with a 76-59 victory over San Diego State University on Monday night at NRG Stadium in Houston.

Senior guard Tristen Newton led UConn (31-8) with 19 points and 10 rebounds while Final Four Most Outstanding Player Adama Sanogo, a junior forward, chipped in with 17 points and 10 rebounds.

It has been revealed that “We weren’t ranked going into the year so we had the chip on our shoulder,” UConn head coach Dan Hurley told game broadcaster CBS. “We knew the level that we could play at, even through those dark times,” he added, referencing the team’s six losses in eight games during the regular season.

He stated going into the tournament his group had confidence garnered during the season.

“And when you have the type of leaders like Andre Jackson (game-high six assists Monday) and Adama Sanogo, they kept this team together, got us back on track and we knew we were the best team in the tournament going in and we just had to play to our level,” he added.

San Diego State (32-7) was topped by Keshad Johnson who had 14 points.

Sources indicate that UConn trailed very early but San Diego State was undone by an 11-minute, eight-second stretch in which they scored just five free throws and missed 12 consecutive shots from the field. The Huskies went from down 10-6 to up 36-24 at halftime.

The Aztecs made a run midway through the second half and narrowed the deficit to five at 60-55 with 5:19 to play but the Huskies scored the next nine to take a comfortable lead into the final two minutes.

“We battled. Battled back to five in the second half, but gave them too much separation,” San Diego State coach Brian Dutcher said. “We had to be at our best. We weren’t at our best. A lot had to do with UConn.”.

Senior guard Adam Seiko told reporters they gave themselves a chance with their second half comeback but UConn “just made a little bit more plays” at the end.

“They have a lot of weapons. They were pretty good,” mentioned Matt Bradley, also a senior guard. “To beat them, we had to make shots. I shot poorly. And you had to have a really good game to beat those dudes on the offensive end.”.

UConn won each of its six tournament games by at least 10 points, with its closest game being a 13-point win over the University of Miami in the national semifinals.

Recent findings suggest that “I just want to thank my teammates, my coaches who believed in me. If it were not for them I would not be here right now,” Sanogo told CBS.

Jordan Hawkins, who scored 16 points for UConn, talked about winning the crown one day after his cousin, Angel Reese of Louisiana State University, won the women’s title.

“I mean it’s absolutely amazing that we both get this opportunity and I mean the family reunion is going to be great so that’s all I know,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that UConn enters rarefied air as only the sixth team to win five NCAA men’s basketball championships, joining UCLA (11), Kentucky (eight), North Carolina (six), Duke (five) and Indiana (five). All of UConn’s titles have come since 1999 with the most recent before Monday occurring in 2014.

UConn’s women’s teams have won 11 basketball national titles.

CNN’s Steve Almasy and Issy Ronald contributed to this report.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scotland women play Sweden in Paisley next Tuesday, with the second leg in Stockholm on 5 December.

Scotland intend to bring fancied Sweden's World Cup dream "crashing down - and do it in a truly Scottish way", according to women's head coach Melissa Andreatta.

Scotland face a two-legged World Cup qualifying play-off against powerhouses Sweden, who are managed by Andreatta's former boss Tony Gustavsson.

The Swedes, who have been semi-finalists at the two previous Women's World Cups and are ranked eighth in the world, will be strong favourites to reach the tournament in Brazil next summer.

Andreatta, who has eight wins, two losses and four draws from her 14 games in charge of Scotland, was Gustavsson's deputy when he was Australia head coach from 2020 to 2024.

While the two have a connection from those years, the Australian is very much in business mode with next week's first leg at St Mirren Park looming.

"A few weeks ago Tony reached out, sent me a few messages and I took my time to respond," she told BBC Scotland.

In a recent development, "It wasn't much about football, just connecting on a personal level - which is probably a good thing, because I can be quite competitive. I just want to focus on business and not the personal level.

"I'm sure, like he is, all we're focused on is how we're going to win.".

Listen to the full interview with Melissa Andreatta.

The Scots finished top of their qualifying group earlier this year after four wins from their six games before beating the Czech Republic 5-2 on aggregate in the play-off semi-final.

That set up the exacting play-off final against the Swedes, a team who narrowly missed out on a spot in the final at the previous two World Cups.

Scotland have made just one appearance at the tournament, in 2019, and Andreatta is excited by the prospect of getting one over her old boss for her new home.

"It's going to be a great occasion to face them at home first," she added.

"They are such a powerhouse nation that carries so much expectation to go to their next tournament. We want to bring that all crashing down and do that in a truly Scottish way. That's what we're going to focus on.

"I definitely won't be looking at their dug out, I'll be focused on us and what we need to do to get the result and go to another tournament.

"They are an exceptional team but we won't be swayed by a team's reputation or ranking.

"We firmly believe that anything is possible. Once that whistle goes, if you've done the work and you're prepared you're in the position to make anything happen. With this group of players and staff I know that's possible, we can take it to anyone on any given day.

In a recent development, "It is a massive challenge but we love those moments and that's why we're here. We've earned it.".

Melissa Andreatta with daughter Mackenzie after Scotland beat the Czech Republic in their World Cup qualification semi-final.

There are more than 10,000 miles between Brisbane - where Andreatta grew up - and Ayr in Scotland, where she now calls home.

While the climate may be vastly different, there's one thing they do have in common - the beach.

According to recent reports, "I love the coastal life. In Australia it's a big part of your lifestyle, being outdoors. I think there's something about the sea, being near it. Relaxing, calming, balancing," she stated.

It has been 18 months since Andreatta was announced as Pedro Martinez Losa's successor as manager of the Scotland women's team and now, with her family alongside her - including two-year-old daughter Mackenzie - she feels at home.

Industry observers note that "We've definitely settled in," she added. "We have the spots that we go to, our routine, we love it here. It's been a great landing spot for us on such a major move.".

But what does her daughter make of her mum's job?

"She's got no idea," says Andreatta. "She just think's mum's on TV. Whenever she sees me she gets excited. Having her at the games is super special, being able to hold her on the pitch. She's such a joy.

"You do these things to make people proud and I want to make her proud.".

Andreatta has made a promising start as Scotland manager - but now faces a huge task.

Scotland without captain Weir for World Cup play-off.

New strategy introduced to transform Scottish women's football over 10 years.

Andreatta was sitting in the pubs of Scotland over the summer as the Tartan Army headed over to the United States in their droves to watch the men's team compete at a first World Cup in almost 30 years.

The women won't have to wait that long if they can book a spot on the plane to Brazil next summer.

Andreatta is hoping to see just as many kilts on the Copacabana beach as there were in the bars of Boston.

"There is a strong desire among the group, not only players but also the staff, there is this desire to make their nation proud and show Scotland that the women's national team belongs here and deserves as much of the limelight as the men's," she added.

In a recent development, "Together we can make our nation proud and what better way to do it? To have our men at the World Cup and then the following summer our women.

"Watching from afar, what the fans did over there and in Boston, why can't we do that in Rio? That's what I'm envisaging but there's a lot to do and achieve before we get there.".

I got to tour SpaceX's Starfactory facility in Starbase, Texas, and what I saw blew my mind

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

STARBASE, Texas  — I just finished covering the Starship Flight 15 mission, and SpaceXs incredible launch tower catch of the returned Ship 42 spacecraft isn't the only thing over the weekend that left me speechless.

The morning of the launch (Nov. 13), SpaceX invited media on a tour of Starbase's Starfactory facility, where it manufactures and assembles both stages of its massive Starship rocket - an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the production and scale of SpaceX's operations, and a glimpse of things to come as Starship notches more and more milestones the more it flies.

For some context, the five-story-tall Starfactory spans approximately 1 million square feet (~93,000 meters), with operations split between Starship's Super Heavy boosters and upper stage Ships, and nearly 330,000 additional square feet (30,000 square meters) of office space. SpaceX officials describe its design as one more akin to an automotive manufacturing plant than that of a typical aerospace production site, and inside, it is absolutely alive with activity.

Sources indicate that we entered through an arch-covered doorway underneath the giant "X" sign on the building's shorter face. Our media gaggle was met with curious glances as we were shown through the doors and guided onto the factory floor - few are ever able to cross that threshold outside of SpaceX employees, and our presence seemed as novel to those busy working as it was to us.

According to recent reports, inside, we were struck with the sheer enormity of Starship's scale. Giant stainless-steel rocket parts were meticulously scattered across different subassembly stations throughout the building, with Ship nose cones, cylindrical sections and booster components all under various stages of manufacture. The sheer quantity of the hardware was staggering, and being so close to each as we walked Starfactory's throughways was an eye-opener.

Starbase is a unique partnership of privately-owned SpaceX property and publicly-accessible land and shoreline, which has created the unique ability for anyone with a mind to do so to drive right up to the the Starship launch pad to see the facilities up close (within a few hundred feet or so, which, as rockets go, is very, very close).

Sources indicate that fully stacked, Starship stands more than 400 feet (120 meters) tall. Standing next to such a towering colossus on the pad is enough to drive home just how major the launch vehicle is, but standing next its segmented components inside Starfactory is even more humbling; like seeing one of Ship's upper aerodynamic flaps, which are each large enough when laid flat that you could park a pair of large SUVs on their faces with room to spare.

Starbase, Texas https://t.co/NqDWwUZXv9August 25, 2025.

Industry observers note that as our tour continued and we passed rows of nose cones under preparation for integration, numbering as high as Ship 51, one stood out from the others. In the distance, only visible for moment between the overlapping views of other Ships as we walked through the production stations, was a nose cone with a series of windows cut out of its face - undoubtedly a prototype for, or possibly even the final article that will be used as NASA's Artemis lunar lander.

In a recent development, NASA has contracted SpaceX to develop a version of Starship capable of landing astronauts on the moon as a part of the agency's Artemis program, and this appeared to the Ship being readied for when that mission arrives. NASA is targeting Artemis IV as the program's first crewed lunar landing in 2028, and while the decision solidifying Starship as the lander tasked with that mission isn't finalized (Blue Origin is also vying for that spot with its Blue Moon lander), SpaceX is clearly operating with the intention of coming out ahead.

In a recent development, but Artemis is clearly not SpaceX's only focus, as evident by the many, many other Ships in production that did not have window holes carved out of them.SpaceX officials said the company is currently completing about one Ship upper stage every two weeks, and one Super Heavy booster every four weeks, with overlapping production allowing multiple rockets to move through the factory simultaneously. The majority of the vehicles currently being assembled will carry stacks of SpaceX's upgraded Starlink Version 3 (V3) satellites.

The firm's Starlink network in low Earth orbit presently consists of more than 11,000 spacecraft beaming wireless internet to SpaceX customers across the globe. All of those were launched on SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 rocket, with the exception of a few more than 50 delivered on Starship's two most recent test flights. Both carried V3 Starlink stacks to add to the constellation, which SpaceX officials say each added the data capacity equivalent to ten Falcon 9 Starlink debuts. And, as they fine tune Starship's design, SpaceX looks to increase the vehicle's launch cadence dramatically, growing the Starlink network as it does.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has stated the organization hopes to launch Starship about once a week beginning in 2027, and with the number of Ships we saw lined up inside Starfactory, launch vehicle inventory doesn't seem like it will be to blame if that goal isn't realized.

SpaceX has adopted a manufacturing process modeled after the automotive industry, where efficiency and reproduction allow for the manufacture of large numbers of identical parts. Automation is a critical part of that process, but not one SpaceX is ready to entirely rely on.

Much of the equipment and tools being used for Starship's production were designed by SpaceX engineers, who are constantly refining production processes to eliminate bottlenecks. And SpaceX has deliberately kept technicians on the floor as Starship's design continues to evolve, rather than automating procedures that might soon become obsolete.

Our tour guide compared SpaceX's manufacturing consistency goals to that of Lego bricks, which are famously precise in their production down to the micro-millimeter accuracy of what now number more than 1 trillion bricks made since the toy firm began in the 1940s.

Recent findings suggest that exiting the far side of the building, we stood in the shadow of SpaceX's two towering Mega Bays, where the sections of Starship are stacked and integrated with their engines - there's one hanger for Ship, and another for Super Heavy. Each can hold about five or six assemblies, and housed two or three vehicles at the time our tour was brought by.

Industry observers note that both Mega Bays, however, looked small against the adjacent Gigabay SpaceX is at the moment constructing. At approximately 700,000 square feet (65,000 square meters), Gigabay will be equipped with room to accommodate up to 24 vehicles at a time, and will facilitate a major increase in SpaceX's ability to assemble its Ship and Super Heavy rockets.

Part of SpaceX's goal with Starship is to make all of what we got to see completely routine; to make rocket debuts and landings as ordinary as commercial airline flights. Still, standing inside Starfactory, surrounded on all sides by huge spacecraft in various stages of assembly, it was hard to imagine a reality where giant rockets flying to and from space on a regular basis wouldn't feel like science fiction.

Later that day a giant rocket launched to outer space - Super Heavy did attempt a return to pad, but was diverted for an offshore landing instead, where it exploded. But the next day, Ship 42 came plunging through the overcast cloud cover, falling belly-first toward the same tower it left just a couple dozen hours before. And then it lit its engines and was caught by the tower.

That felt like science fiction too.

Josh Dinner is Space.com's Spaceflight Staff Writer and a photographer with a passion for science and exploration. He has worked the space beat since 2016, covering the evolution of NASA's commercial spaceflight partnerships and crewed missions, planetary science missions, the Artemis program and humanity's return to the moon. He also enjoys building 1:144-scale model rockets and spacecraft. Find some of Josh's launch photography on Instagram, and follow him on X, where he mostly posts in haiku.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

In the modern Manchester United, it sometimes seems that the bad news comes ever sooner after the good. There is less time to enjoy it before the unwanted reality check. So it was that, when much of Sky Sports descended on Carrington on Friday and chief executive Omar Berrada revealed they were in talks with Bruno Fernandes about a latest deal, the question was put to the captain.

According to recent reports, “The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, reveals that they want me to stay,” he said. And if it was a partial answer, saying that the club were keen to extend their relationship but not revealing if he was, nor was there much encouragement to be derived from his explanation. “I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.”.

Industry observers note that A couple of days later came a result to underline the wisdom of waiting. Sunday’s 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool increased the chances United will be in the Championship, rather than the Champions League, next season. At the least, Fernandes should put his future on hold before working out which division they will be in.

It has been revealed that his next transfer may come next summer, when his contract expires – though United have the option to extend it by a further year – but his last move remains his January 2020 switch from Sporting CP. Wednesday night gives him a first chance return to his former club. It could be a triumphant comeback: Fernandes remains among Sporting’s greatest exports and he is still the only unqualified success in United’s recruitment since Sir Alex Ferguson retired.

It was at Sporting that he started scoring at a rate that is almost unrivalled among midfielders: 33 goals in the 2018-19 season, a further 15 in a few months before United made their move.

Almost seven years on, Fernandes goes back on the brink of milestones: one away from a century of Portugal caps, a hat-trick short of 200 club career goals, the last 113 of them for United.

But individual achievements seem to outnumber the collective feats. That is no criticism: at times it has felt as though Fernandes has prevented things from getting worse for United. He has won the FA Cup and the Carabao Cup but, in other eras, that would not be much to show for seven seasons at Old Trafford.

It has been revealed that he won the PFA Player of the Year and Footballer of the Year awards last season; they had the air of lifetime achievement awards, as much as recognition for his record-breaking tally of 21 Premier League assists. He has won United’s player-of-the-year award a record five times: but previously, there was more competition. Paul Scholes, for example, never won it.

The contrarian notion United would be better off without him looks increasingly fanciful when the shortcomings of others are ever more apparent. Fernandes has a petulant streak and a capacity to give the ball away in his attempts to make something happen; yet when he criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics after the defeat to Como and the manager responding by benching his skipper, United were hopeless against Bournemouth.

Industry observers note that mauricio Pochettino marked his arrival at Old Trafford by confirming Fernandes as hius captain. He has now worn the armband under eight managers or caretakers – Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Ralf Rangnick, Erik ten Hag, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Ruben Amorim, Darren Fletcher, Carrick and Pochettino – whereas arguably United’s greatest captain, Roy Keane, only did so under one.

According to recent reports, it is another indication of instability and underachievement. As Fernandes implied on Friday, he has made sacrifices to stay at United. He could have had a warmer climate elsewhere, he said. He could have made more money, too: the Saudi Pro-League, in particular, would have been more lucrative. Galatasaray might have been.

Industry observers note that the sense, perhaps, is that Fernandes, more than United, has to decide what comes next. In footballing lexicon, players earn fresh contracts. Maybe, though, the club have to earn the right for a deal that is proffered to be signed.

Fernandes will turn 33 next September. His next contract will probably be the last at anything near his peak, even for a man who, since the start of the 2017-18 season, has averaged over 60 games a year for club and country.

And yet, he may note, he might have played more in the Champions League simply by staying at Sporting. They were quarter-finalists last season, when United were not in the competition. They are three points ahead of United now. They stand a far better chance of being in the Champions League next season.

Sources indicate that fernandes has been one of the most visible faces in the decline of United, but also the man who did more than anyone else to fight it. It has given him a form of greatness but perhaps, as he returns to Portugal, it could make him ponder the career choices he has made, and will make.

Latest Update: Can returning Beattie and Haughey make an impact?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Beattie won the last of her 13 caps last year while the uncapped Haughey was last called into the senior squad in 2021.
  • Michael McArdle has decided the upcoming friendly double-header against Greece is the perfect time to bring back Kerry Beattie and Ella Haughey from the international wilderness.
  • Glentoran midfielder Chloe McCarron is also in under McArdle for the first time after a lengthily absence, but the Glentoran midfielder would likely have been included sooner if not for a spell on the sidelines through injury.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Beattie won the last of her 13 caps last year while the uncapped Haughey was last called into the senior squad in 2021.

Michael McArdle has decided the upcoming friendly double-header against Greece is the perfect time to bring back Kerry Beattie and Ella Haughey from the international wilderness.

Glentoran midfielder Chloe McCarron is also in under McArdle for the first time after a lengthily absence, but the Glentoran midfielder would likely have been included sooner if not for a spell on the sidelines through injury.

Beattie won her last cap a year ago while Haughey will hope to make a senior debut in one of the two games against Greece at Inver Park after she was an unused substitute in friendlies against England and Scotland in her sole call up in 2021.

The inclusion of both players, who have been in good form at their clubs, shows McArdle is willing to keep the door open for a return to the international squad if players are performing at club level.

Magill returns to NI squad for Greece friendlies.

Beattie has four goals in her 13 NI caps.

Portsmouth striker Beattie has been in and out of squads since her debut in 2021.

The 24-year-old has four goals in 13 caps, the last of which she won against Iceland in the Nations League play-off a year ago.

A prolific forward during two spells at Glentoran, she has struggled for consistency in moves across to Scotland with the likes of Glasgow City, Hearts and Aberdeen.

She left the Dons in the summer and consulted with McArdle when deciding upon her next move, before joining WSL 2 side Portsmouth.

Beattie has eight goals in all competitions for a Pompey side languishing at the bottom of the table and McArdle is pleased she has settled in well.

"Kerry had spells at Hearts and Aberdeen and for whatever reason it didn't quite work out at both, she had good spells but not a consistent run to express herself," McArdle said.

Sources indicate that "The move to Portsmouth, I was delighted she reached out to me for some advice, it's an alignment for her and it's been a great move on and off the pitch. It's allowed her to enjoy herself but also play 90 minutes and be that focal point striker.

"She will have been disappointed not to make the squad for the [World Cup] play-off [against Portugal] with her form but she worked hard and she's back in, I'm delighted for her.".

Beattie faces stiff competition for the starting striker role from the likes of returning captain Simone Magill and Kess Elmore, who impressed in the last camp and scored against Portugal, but she should receive some minutes across the two games and will be keen to grasp her chance to make an impact.

Left-back Haughey was called up to the senior squad as a 16-year-old under Kenny Shiels, but did not feature.

West Brom defender Haughey's last involvement with NI came when she represented the under-19s in 2023.

A Lisburn Rangers player when Kenny Shiels included her in the senior squad as a 16-year-old, Haughey then moved to Nottingham Forest before settling at the Baggies, who play in the National League.

The left-back, 22, has been a regular this season for the club in the third tier and combines playing with her university studies.

Left-back has been a problem position for NI which McArdle has been trying to address as demonstrated by him bringing in Lucy-Jayne Grant in the last camp and Haughey for this window to allow Rebecca Holloway to play as a central defender.

Haughey will be competing with Grant to fill that full-back role on the left side and McArdle believes she is more than capable of doing so having tried to bring her back into the squad earlier in his reign.

"Ella's been at West Brom for a few years now. She has real potential, strong, athletic potential. We tried to call her up sooner but there were some challenges," he explained.

"She's probably been one of their top performers and one of the top performers in the league. Delighted she's earned this opportunity and hopefully she can make her debut and achieve her first cap.".

McArdle has made a concerted to continue to widen the player pool available to him as he aims to build depth ahead of the Nations League campaign next year, but if Beattie and Haughey catch the eye it will show that giving chances to those previously involved under different managers could be another possibility.

Hexed review: Turning Red meets Harry Potter, minus the problematic politics

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spooky season lives on as Disney unfurls Hexed, a witches' tale opening over the Thanksgiving holiday.
  • In a recent development, co-directed by Jason Hand, Fawn Veerasunthorn, and Josie Trinidad, Hexed offers a story about a child destined for greatness.
  • This combination mixes the coming-of-age comedy and mother-daughter drama of Turning Red with a magical realm reminiscent of Harry Potter (and the underrated Disney show Owl House), creating an entertaining elixir that's fun, imaginative, and moving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spooky season lives on as Disney unfurls Hexed, a witches' tale opening over the Thanksgiving holiday. And lucky us, their latest is a magical adventure that might pull some inspiration from Harry Potter, but in a fresh and fun way (that doesn't line the pockets of unrepentant transphobe J.K. Rowling).

In a recent development, co-directed by Jason Hand, Fawn Veerasunthorn, and Josie Trinidad, Hexed offers a story about a child destined for greatness. However, her path to mastering magic is marred by an evil, power-hungry fascist who is surrounded by a flock of vicious mythical beasts. However, rather than focusing on a sad orphan in England, Hexed's Potter-like tale centers on the Ohio-raised daughter of a mother whose love language is smothering.

This combination mixes the coming-of-age comedy and mother-daughter drama of Turning Red with a magical realm reminiscent of Harry Potter (and the underrated Disney show Owl House), creating an entertaining elixir that's fun, imaginative, and moving.

According to recent reports, hailee Steinfeld lends her voice to Billie Doe, a teen girl introduced through a heist in which she steals her high school's mascot (a befuddled owl) so he can be set free. This seemingly bad behavior — which includes "borrowing" her mom's car without a driver's license — is more than an act of rebellion against school uniforms, her grumbling principal (Brett Gelman), or her overprotective mother, Alice (Rashida Jones). Scored by Queen's rapturous anthem "I Want to Break Free," it's a symbolic act that plays as this Disney heroine's "I wish" song, though this Disney heroine doesn't get an original song of her own. Billie wants to be free to spread her wings and be herself.

It has been revealed that for years, Billie's mother has given her endless "guidelines," building around her a world of rules from which Billie is desperate to escape. So, when a magical portal opens in her bedroom, of course she rushes on through without looking back. But this won't be a story where Billie pulls a Dorothy Gale in Oz, wandering around alone while her mother figure Auntie Em is none the wiser. Shortly after Billie has tumbled into the magical realm of Hexe and made a spectacle out of herself by flying with style, her mother Alice follows.

Together, they will battle against the vicious Queen Celeste (Jodie Foster), and her fleet of half-raven/half-human Morphlings. (Imagine if the Wicked Witch's flying monkeys were chic, side-eyeing goth girls with shapeshifting abilities). But to join forces, they first have to understand each other, literally traveling into each other's minds to see each other's perspectives. That's a bit of magic we could all use.

According to recent reports, bound to Billie, we're quickly made aware that she doesn't fit in. A school photo shows her not only off in the corner with a glum look on her face as the other kids smile in unison, but also with more vibrantly colored hair and skin that sets her apart. She's not regarded as beautiful for this, but strange and worthy of shunning.

Sources indicate that she loves plants, attracts stray cats, and possesses a reckless streak that makes her one of the rowdiest Disney heroines since The Little Mermaid. And while her classmates might scoff and her teachers might sneer, Billie is dedicated to being herself. But when her mother sneers at her, she almost literally shrinks.

In a recent development, it hurts to believe your mother sees you as a screw-up. This significant feeling becomes a crucial incentive for three of the film's lead characters, having sprawling consequences. Maybe we can't choose to not be hurt by a parent's rejection. But we can choose how we respond. Will we cave to their pressure? Will we dull our own shine or corrupt our hearts to distort ourselves to meet their expectations? Or will we soar above?

The plotline of mothers and teen daughters struggling to see each other outside of the parenthood dynamic puts Hexed on the same path as Brave and Turning Red. In each of these Disney animated films, the mother seems cold as she urges her daughter to assimilate to societal norms. But in each instance, it's with the goal of protecting her from hardship.

It has been revealed that however, Hexed gives deeper space to the idea that being forced to be like everyone else by the very person who should believe you are special is its own kind of hell. And it's not one invented with each newly introduced generation, but a trauma that can reach back, scarring those who come after.

For this intense central drama and all its macabre elements, Hexed is nonstop entertaining. Steinfeld recaptures the teen angst and rebellious spirit she indicated in the phenomenal live-action coming-of-age comedy The Edge of Seventeen. Jones brings her wry wit to Alice, while Foster's sharpness cuts like a knife through velvet. You can practically hear her targets' self-esteem being shredded to ribbons.

In a recent development, while there's plenty of noteworthy names in the ensemble cast, including Dan Stevens, Tracey Ullman, Randall Park, Stephen Fry, and Henry Winkler, it's Fallout's Walton Goggins who proves an unrepentant scene-stealer. Slathering on a Cajun accent like it's barbecue sauce, Goggins brings a surly but sweet attitude to a three-eyed cat familiar named Beef Roger Crummchuk. If that name alone has you intrigued, you'll love Hexed. Chaotic, intriguing, and silly, this character's name is a solid distillation of the movie itself. Plus, Goggins and Steinfeld have terrific chemistry as an overeager protégé and a wizened mentor.

Recent findings suggest that the filmmakers have bypassed the typically clean Disney aesthetic, which demands its heroines be soft, round, and always pretty, and worked in some alt elements to give Billie an easy-to-clock baby goth look. In a beautiful and meaningful element of the movie's color story, the teals and fuchsias that Billie favors in her Ohio life are reflected in Hexe, along with golds and purples that all suggest she belongs, as she visually fits in this world she's never known. But when it comes to the colors of the queen, they are chillier, more muted, speaking not only to the difference between heroine and villainess, but also to the distinction in their energies.

With a spirited sense of humor and a pop music soundtrack, Hexed brings an inviting verve to its story of generational trauma. And in that, it helps the spoonful of medicine go down, for the children and parents in the audience alike. For those kids not old enough to be having this kind of psychological connection to Hexed, they'll be delighted with the daffy physical humor, rousing action sequences, and an array of colorful characters who'll frighten and delight. Hexed is spell-binding.

Bayern Munich have insisted that Jamal Musiala’s health remains their "top priority" following a "constructive meeting" with representatives of the 23-year-old midfielder.

According to recent reports, earlier this year, the player collapsed on two occasions within four days during pre-season fixtures. It was subsequently disclosed that he was suffering from absence seizures linked to a form of "neurological dysfunction".

The German club faced scrutiny over their handling of the matter after public remarks from senior figures. Honorary president Uli Hoeness questioned if Musiala would "regain the performance level he once had", suggesting his 2025 contract might no longer match his potential on-pitch contributions.

Similar doubts were voiced by member of the supervisor board Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who proposed renegotiating the agreement, while chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen questioned the deal, should Musiala struggle to recover his peak conditioning.

These comments drew criticism from global players’ union FIFPRO, which voiced concern over repeated public remarks challenging the player's contract, saying that "a club of Bayern’s standing should know better".

Responding on Wednesday after Tuesday's discussions, Bayern sought to clarify their position in a joint patch with Musiala's agency, 11WINS.

The club stated: "Yesterday, Tuesday, FC Bayern Munich held a constructive meeting with Jamal Musiala’s management. The player’s health is the top priority for both parties. Jamal Musiala will receive full support throughout his recovery.

In a recent development, "Following numerous rumours over the past few days, FC Bayern and 11WINS, the agency representing Jamal Musiala, would like to clarify the following: Jamal Musiala was first examined for symptoms resembling absence seizures on 22 April 2025. This examination took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical department, immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared.

"FC Bayern and Jamal Musiala’s management have agreed to continue their discussions in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality.".

On the pitch, Musiala returned as a substitute during last Friday's 1-1 draw against Cologne, marking his first outing since September after recovering from a hamstring injury. He has also been selected in Bayern's squad to play Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 2,500-year-old Parthenon is ancient Greece's most notable temple and is regarded as one of the greatest masterpieces of the High Classical period of Greek art.
  • Dedicated to Athena, the city's patron goddess, it towers over Athens from its position on the Acropolis — a powerful symbol of the city's importance.
  • Industry observers note that the Parthenon had a lasting influence on Western ideas of humanity and art.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2,500-year-old Parthenon is ancient Greece's most notable temple and is regarded as one of the greatest masterpieces of the High Classical period of Greek art.

Dedicated to Athena, the city's patron goddess, it towers over Athens from its position on the Acropolis — a powerful symbol of the city's importance.

Industry observers note that the Parthenon had a lasting influence on Western ideas of humanity and art. The sculptures adorning its pediments, created under the direction of the legendary sculptor Phidias, are considered unparalleled examples of proportion and grace. They have influenced artists from ancient Rome through Neoclassicism to the modern era.

In a recent development, the east pediment above the temple entrance depicted the birth of the goddess Athena from the head of her father Zeus, surrounded by the Olympian gods. A total of 39 figures adorned the roughly 29-meter-long work of art. At its center stood a colossal Zeus figure, measuring 3.8 meters in height.

For centuries, scholars have puzzled over exactly what the arrangement looked like, as the pediment was destroyed during the Christianization of Greece.

But now there has been a breakthrough.

After decades of painstaking detective work and with the help of modern technology, archaeologist Vinzenz Brinkmann and his team have managed to piece together all the surviving fragments of the Parthenon's east pediment.

Industry observers note that brinkmann heads the Antiquities and Asia department at Frankfurt's Liebieghaus sculpture collection. "We're very, very confident that we've solved the mystery," he told DW.

The results are now on display in an exhibition at the Liebieghaus titled "Athena, the Stage is Yours: The Parthenon Puzzle.".

Only around 20% of the original marble sculpture's volume is known to have survived. The fragments are scattered across various European museums, with most located in Athens. The British Museum also holds numerous pieces.

Brinkmann and his wife, Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann, have spent more than 40 years working on this ancient puzzle, with so many of its pieces missing.

And they were far from the first to attempt it: "Already in the 19th century, many scholars studied the subject and developed well-founded theories based on their deep knowledge of ancient sources," Brinkmann explains.

Industry observers note that in 1910, a study documenting the many fragments held by the British Museum was published. The research team was able to build on that earlier work, but progress remained slow for years.

Then, in 2014, a visit to the Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg provided Brinkmann with a crucial clue. There, he encountered a Roman sarcophagus featuring a relief of Athena's birth. "That's when it suddenly clicked: They're all there!".

Nine such sarcophagi are known to exist, almost all of them in Rome. Each depicts a different section of the Parthenon's east pediment.

Brinkmann emphasizes that other scholars had already noticed this connection in the 19th century. "But we really seized on the idea and never let go.".

The researchers also benefited from 21st-century technology: 3D scanners and printers. Brinkmann and his team visited numerous destinations to examine around 60 original fragments at different locations — traveling light. An iPhone was all they needed to scan the pieces.

Industry observers note that digitally fitting the fragments together led to another key discovery. "We know these figures we're putting together!" Brinkmann recalls thinking at the time.

The Romans had repeatedly made individual copies of all the sculptures from the pediment. "These copies matched the fragments perfectly. Suddenly, we found ourselves surrounded by old acquaintances we had never suspected had come from the pediment." This finally enabled the researchers to reconstruct all the figures and their original arrangement.

Industry observers note that using a 3D printer, the team created a 4-meter-long model at a scale of 1:7.7. For the exhibition, they also produced life-size 3D prints of the most vital fragments and mounted them on panels depicting the complete figures at their original size. An animation brings the reconstructed composition to life, digitally assembling the fragments to reveal how the east pediment once looked.

Alongside works from the Liebieghaus collection, the exhibition features loans from other institutions, including the Vatican Museums and the Louvre. Objects from the Acropolis Museum in Athens had originally been expected as well. But Greece withdrew its participation after learning that the British Museum was also planning to lend fragments to the Frankfurt exhibition. The Liebieghaus ultimately decided to forgo the British-owned fragments, too.

There is a reason for this controversy. Britain holds a substantial portion of the Parthenon frieze as well as fragments from both pediments.

Greek authorities have been campaigning for their return for decades.

In Britain, the 56 sections of the frieze are known as the "Elgin Marbles," named after Lord Elgin, the British ambassador to the Ottoman Empire in Constantinople.

In the early 19th century, Elgin had sculptures removed from the exterior of the Parthenon on the Acropolis in Athens. They were taken to Britain with the consent of the Ottoman Empire, which ruled Greece at the time.

Britain maintains that the sculptures were legally acquired.

Greece, however, considers them stolen.

According to recent reports, for years, the dispute remained deadlocked. Since the Labour Party came to power in Britain, there has been some movement toward resolving it. But apparently not enough to persuade Greece to lend artworks to an exhibition in which the British Museum might also participate.

The exhibition "Athena, the Stage is Yours. The Parthenon Puzzle" runs through July 25, 2027, at the Liebieghaus in Frankfurt.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.
  • It will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the United Kingdom since the men's tournament in 1966.
  • The four countries were the only bidders for the tournament, and were ratified as co-hosts at a specially arranged virtual meeting from Fifa's Zurich headquarters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spain beat England 1-0 to win the 2023 World Cup.

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.

It will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the United Kingdom since the men's tournament in 1966.

The four countries were the only bidders for the tournament, and were ratified as co-hosts at a specially arranged virtual meeting from Fifa's Zurich headquarters.

The tournament will consist of 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.

The 'All Together' bid included a proposal to use 19 venues, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.

Monday's special meeting of Fifa's Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

The news comes on the same day the UK government revealed a vision for one million more girls to play, watch or be in leadership roles in sport by the time the tournament takes place.

Hosting World Cup means decade of excitement - Weir.

Fifa announces UK will host 2035 Women's World Cup.

England failed to win the right to host the men's World Cups in 2006 and 2018, and a proposed UK and Ireland bid for the 2030 tournament was abandoned.

But England and Scotland hosted matches at the men's Euros in 2021, and England staged the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.

England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the men's European Championship in 2028.

Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.

"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.".

The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.

If Manchester United's proposed fresh Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it would still be considered in its current form.

Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium are the two Welsh venues, with Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow in Scotland.

Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government mentioned in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.

A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's upcoming Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.

Fifa is yet to decide whether all four co-hosts will qualify automatically.

The Principality Stadium in Cardiff is one of two Welsh venues, along with the Cardiff City Stadium.

The participation of women and girls in football has risen by 2.3m since the Women's European Championship was held in England in 2022.

However, women remain significantly underrepresented in leadership positions.

Only a quarter of chief executive, chair or performance director roles in major UK sports are held by women and only 12% of sports federations are led by a female.

Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, said: "This is a proud day for Welsh football.

"We've put forward Wrexham and Cardiff as host cities, and it's exciting to think what a World Cup could bring to both cities and the communities around them.

Sources indicate that "In Llunio Cymru - our 10-year strategy - we've set ourselves the ambition of reaching the knockout stages in 2035. Some of the players who could take us there are learning the game at clubs across Wales today. Our job is to make sure that wherever a girl grows up in Wales, she can find a team close to home, have a coach who helps her develop and see a route to the Cymru shirt.".

Irish Football Association chief executive Patrick Nelson said the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country".

"Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that," he added.

Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell said hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".

Recent findings suggest that he added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come.".

It has been revealed that fifa's evaluation, published earlier this month, rated the bid 4.3 out of five. Its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".

That is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.

The bid evaluation remarked: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.

"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.

"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues.".
